definition_zh: 憎恶；痛恨；深恶痛绝
definition_en: to dislike something very much and regard it as hateful
core_image: 看到某物就眉头紧锁、连连后退的厌恶表情
scene: 奶奶站在院子门口，看着工人把老树连根挖走，气得手都在抖。She absolutely abominates any cruelty to animals.
sceneCN: 这里 abominate 是「痛恨、深恶痛绝」（第 1 个义项：对残忍行为强烈憎恶）；句意为她绝对痛恨任何虐待动物的行为。

derivatives.zh: 由动词加名词后缀构成，义为「憎恶之物；可憎的事」
由动词加形容词后缀构成，义为「可憎的；恶劣的」
由形容词加副词后缀构成，义为「可憎地；恶劣地」

senses.title: To hate something deeply
senses.definition: to feel intense hatred or disgust for something, especially on moral grounds
senses.definitionCN: 对某事物怀有强烈憎恨或厌恶，尤指出于道德立场
senses.example: Most reformers abominated the slave trade and fought to end it.
senses.exampleCN: 大多数改革者痛恨奴隶贸易，并为之斗争到底。
senses.why: The Latin root ab- (away) plus omin- (omen) suggests pushing something away as a bad omen, which grew into strong moral loathing.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁词根 ab-（离开）加 omin-（预兆），本义是把不祥之物推得远远的，由此长出强烈的道德憎恶。

senses.title: To regard as abhorrent or shameful
senses.definition: to consider something so offensive that it must be rejected outright
senses.definitionCN: 认为某事物恶劣到必须彻底拒斥
senses.example: The old professor abominated sloppy arguments in academic writing.
senses.exampleCN: 老教授对学术写作中敷衍的论证深恶痛绝。
senses.why: Once something is marked as an ill omen, it becomes shameful in the community, so the verb extends from personal disgust to public condemnation.
senses.whyCN: 事物一旦被标为凶兆，在群体中便成为可耻，动词因此从个人厌恶扩展到公开谴责。

intro.en: Abominate comes from Latin abominari, formed on ab- 'away from' and omen 'omen', literally 'to deprecate as an ill omen'.
intro.cn: abominate 来自拉丁语 abominari，由 ab-「远离」加 omen「预兆」构成，本义为「当作凶兆加以拒斥」。

items.en: Omen meant a sign, usually warning of what is to come.
items.cn: omen 指预兆，通常是预示将来的信号。

items.en: Abominari meant to ward off as an unfavorable omen, literally to turn something away.
items.cn: abominari 义为把不祥之兆挡开，字面即「把某物推开」。

items.en: A folk association with ab homine 'away from man, inhuman' reinforced the sense of what decent people reject.
items.cn: 民间将其与 ab homine「远离人、非人」相联系，强化了「正派人所拒斥之物」的语义。

items.en: Abominable passed through French before the verb form settled in English.
items.cn: abominable 一词先经法语传入，动词形式随后在英语定型。

items.en: Both adjective and verb entered English in religious and moral contexts, condemning sin and cruelty.
items.cn: 形容词与动词都在宗教与道德语境中进入英语，用于谴责罪恶与残忍。

items.en: The verb is now formal and rare, kept mostly in written moral argument, while abominable and abomination remain common.
items.cn: 动词如今正式而少见，多见于书面道德论说，而 abominable 与 abomination 仍常用。

note.en: The first group gathers the omen family; the second lists verbs of strong moral dislike.
note.cn: 第一组是 omen 词族；第二组是表示强烈道德憎恶的动词。

entries.definition: a thing or practice that is loathsome; the noun partner of this verb.
entries.definitionCN: 令人憎恶的事物或行为；本词的名词形式。

entries.definition: detestable or shockingly bad, as in abominable weather.
entries.definitionCN: 可憎的或恶劣透顶的，如 abominable weather。

entries.definition: signaling that something bad is likely to happen; shares the omen root.
entries.definitionCN: 预示不祥的；与本词同享 omen 词根，但只是同根而非近义。

entries.definition: not typical or regular; only looks similar because of the ab- prefix, different root.
entries.definitionCN: 不正常的；只因 ab- 前缀而形似，词根完全不同。

entries.definition: to hate something strongly; the everyday counterpart of this formal verb.
entries.definitionCN: 强烈憎恨；是本正式动词的日常对应词。

entries.definition: to feel revulsion or intense dislike for someone or something.
entries.definitionCN: 对某人或某物感到强烈反感与厌恶。

entries.definition: to reject something with horror, often on moral grounds.
entries.definitionCN: 出于道德上的反感而拒斥某事物。

entries.definition: to curse or express abhorrence of something, very formal and rare.
entries.definitionCN: 诅咒或表达对某物的憎恨，极为正式少见。

entries.definition: to love deeply; the emotional opposite of abominate.
entries.definitionCN: 深爱；是 abominate 的情感反义。

normalIntro.en: Build the word from its Latin parts and family.
normalIntro.cn: 从拉丁部件与词族入手记忆本词。

normal.en: ab- means away, so you push the thing away.
normal.cn: ab- 表示「离开」，即把可憎之物推开。

normal.en: omin- is the root of omen, an ill omen must be avoided.
normal.cn: omin- 是 omen（预兆）的词根，凶兆必被避拒。

normal.en: Family: abominable, abomination — same sense of hatefulness.
normal.cn: 词族：abominable、abomination，都含「可憎」之义。

normal.en: The -ate ending marks it as a verb of attitude.
normal.cn: -ate 后缀标记这是一个表态度的动词。

normal.en: Opposite pairing: abominate vs. adore, hate away vs. love toward.
normal.cn: 反向配对：abominate 对 adore，推离对倾心。

abstract.en: Picture slamming a window on something monstrous.
abstract.cn: 想象对着怪物猛地关上窗户。

abstract.en: Feel the shudder of turning away from a bad omen.
abstract.cn: 体会转身避开凶兆时那阵战栗。

abstract.en: See the word as a door slammed shut on what you hate.
abstract.cn: 把这个词看成对憎恶之物砰然关闭的门。

examples.en: Environmentalists abominate the careless dumping of industrial waste.
examples.cn: 环保人士痛恨工业废料的随意倾倒。

examples.en: He abominated the noise of the city and moved to the mountains.
examples.cn: 他厌恶城市的嘈杂，搬去了山里。

examples.en: The treaty showed that both nations abominated the use of chemical weapons.
examples.cn: 条约表明两国都对使用化学武器深恶痛绝。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「饿泼米泥贴」——看到剩饭泼米撒泥贴在地上，让人憎恶得直皱眉。

root: 拉丁语 abominari：ab-（离开、拒斥）+ omen/omin-（预兆）。本义为「视作凶兆而避拒」，经中世纪拉丁与法语进入英语；语义由「避凶」引申为「道德憎恶」。om- 与形容词 ominous 同根，与 abnormal 等词无词源关系。

sensesIntro.en: From warding off an ill omen, the verb narrows to intense moral hatred of things or practices.
sensesIntro.cn: 动词由「避拒凶兆」收窄为对事物或行为的强烈道德憎恶。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: turning your back and pushing away something loathsome.
core.cn: 核心意象：转身背对，把可憎之物推开。

branches.en: PERSONAL HATE: reformers and private individuals feel intense loathing for cruelty and waste.
branches.cn: 个人憎恶：改革者与个人对残忍、浪费等抱有强烈痛恨。

branches.en: SHAMEFUL REJECTION: the community brands sloppy work or vice as intolerable.
branches.cn: 耻感拒斥：群体把敷衍劣行或恶习标为不可容忍。

branches.en: MORAL GROUND: both senses lean on shared norms rather than mere taste.
branches.cn: 道德基础：两个义项都倚重共同规范，而非单纯口味。

branches.en: FORMAL REGISTER: written argument prefers this verb to plain hate.
branches.cn: 正式语域：书面论说偏爱用此动词而非普通 hate。

branches.en: OPPOSITE POLE: adore and cherish mark the loveward end of the same scale.
branches.cn: 反义一端：adore 与 cherish 位于同一情感尺度的爱慕端。

intro.en: The ab- prefix and the omen root organize a small family of rejection words.
intro.cn: ab- 前缀与 omen 词根构成了一个表拒斥的小词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin relatives keep the ideas of omen and pushing away.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁同族词保留了「预兆」与「推开」的观念。

definition_zh: 可憎之物；憎恶的行为；令人厌恶的事
definition_en: a thing or practice that is loathsome and should be rejected
core_image: 人人避之不及的一摊秽物
scene: 老街坊听说有人要把河边湿地填平盖仓库，都摇头叹气。They called the plan an abomination against nature.
sceneCN: 这里 abomination 是「可憎之行」（第 1 个义项：令人憎恶的计划）；句意为他们称这个计划是违背自然的可憎之举。

pos.zh: 强烈的厌恶感（旧式用法）

senses.title: A loathsome thing or practice
senses.definition: a thing, custom, or act regarded as vile and deserving condemnation
senses.definitionCN: 被视为卑劣、应受谴责的事物、习俗或行为
senses.example: The report called child trafficking an abomination that no law should tolerate.
senses.exampleCN: 报告称贩卖儿童是任何法律都不应容忍的可憎罪行。
senses.why: The omen root marks the thing as ill and pushed away, so the noun names whatever the community turns from.
senses.whyCN: 预兆词根把该物标为凶恶、须被推开，名词因此指群体共同背弃之物。

senses.title: Intense disgust or hatred
senses.definition: the feeling of loathing itself, chiefly in the older phrase hold something in abomination
senses.definitionCN: 憎恶之情本身，主要用于旧式短语 hold something in abomination
senses.example: Victorian readers held cruelty in abomination and wrote to protest it.
senses.exampleCN: 维多利亚时代的读者对残忍深恶痛绝，纷纷撰文抗议。
senses.why: A rejected thing first provokes a feeling; English kept the feeling sense inside one fixed older phrase.
senses.whyCN: 被拒斥之物先激起情感；英语把这种情感义保留在一个固定的旧式短语里。

senses.title: Something outrageously bad in quality
senses.definition: something shockingly poor or badly made, often said of tasteless work
senses.definitionCN: 品质恶劣或做工糟糕之物，常用于评价粗劣的作品
senses.example: Critics dismissed the new tower as an architectural abomination.
senses.exampleCN: 评论家斥那座新塔为建筑上的败笔。
senses.why: When moral hate loses its object, the word drifts to anything that offends taste or standards.
senses.whyCN: 当道德憎恶失去对象，词义便漂移到任何冒犯品味或标准之物。

intro.en: Abomination comes from Latin abominatio, the noun of abominari 'to deprecate as an ill omen', from ab- 'away' plus omen.
intro.cn: abomination 来自拉丁语 abominatio，是 abominari「视作凶兆而避拒」的名词，由 ab-「离开」加 omen「预兆」构成。

items.en: Omen named a sign of things to come, feared when unfavorable.
items.cn: omen 指预示未来的征兆，不吉时令人畏惧。

items.en: Abominari meant to ward off or condemn as an ill omen.
items.cn: abominari 义为把不祥之兆挡开或加以谴责。

items.en: A popular link with ab homine 'inhuman' made the word a label for what decent people reject.
items.cn: 民间联想 ab homine「非人」，使此词成为正派人所拒之物的标签。

items.en: Abominacion passed into French carrying both the thing and the feeling.
items.cn: abominacion 进入法语，同时承载「可憎之物」与「憎恶之情」两义。

items.en: The word arrived in religious prose, condemning sin before spreading to moral and aesthetic judgement.
items.cn: 该词经宗教散文进入英语，先谴责罪孽，后扩展到道德与审美评判。

items.en: Today it names anything execrable, from cruelty to ugly buildings, keeping its formal tone.
items.cn: 如今它指一切可憎之事，从残忍到丑陋建筑，仍保持正式语气。

note.en: The first group shows the omen family; the second lists nouns of strong dislike or badness.
note.cn: 第一组为 omen 词族；第二组为表强烈憎恶或恶劣的名词。

entries.definition: to hate deeply; the verb from which this noun is drawn.
entries.definitionCN: 深恶痛绝；本名词所自出的动词。

entries.definition: detestable or shockingly bad.
entries.definitionCN: 可憎的；恶劣透顶的。

entries.definition: giving a warning of bad things to come; shares omen, not the sense of hate.
entries.definitionCN: 不祥的；同享 omen 词根，但并无憎恶之义。

entries.definition: a class, name, or religious group; looks similar but has a different root.
entries.definitionCN: 类别、名称或教派；拼写相似但词根不同。

entries.definition: an extremely cruel, violent act; the stress is on cruelty rather than religious disgust.
entries.definitionCN: 极端残忍的暴行；重在残暴而非宗教式憎恶。

entries.definition: something detested or cursed, once a church ban.
entries.definitionCN: 遭憎恶或诅咒之物，原为教会禁令用语。

entries.definition: a grotesquely bad or unnatural thing, often physical.
entries.definitionCN: 怪异丑陋、不自然之物，常指实体。

entries.definition: strong disapproval mixed with revulsion; names the feeling, not the object.
entries.definitionCN: 强烈的反感与厌恶；指情感本身而非对象。

entries.definition: great pleasure; the emotional opposite pole.
entries.definitionCN: 极大快乐；情感上的对立端。

normalIntro.en: Use the shared omen root and the word family.
normalIntro.cn: 利用共同的 omen 词根与词族记忆。

normal.en: ab- pushes the ill thing away; -tion makes it a noun.
normal.cn: ab- 推开凶恶之物；-tion 使之成为名词。

normal.en: omen inside the word: a bad omen to be avoided.
normal.cn: 词中含 omen：须避拒的凶兆。

normal.en: Family chain: abominate (verb) → abomination (thing) → abominable (adjective).
normal.cn: 词族链：abominate（动词）→ abomination（物）→ abominable（形容词）。

normal.en: Fixed phrase: hold something in abomination equals loathe.
normal.cn: 固定短语：hold something in abomination 即「深恶」。

normal.en: Contrast with ominous: same root, warning vs. loathing.
normal.cn: 与 ominous 对照：同根，一表预警一表憎恶。

abstract.en: Picture the whole village turning its back on one thing.
abstract.cn: 想象全村人齐齐背对同一件事。

abstract.en: Feel the cold shiver when a dark omen appears.
abstract.cn: 体会凶兆出现时脊背发凉之感。

abstract.en: See the word as a label pasted on what must not exist.
abstract.cn: 把该词看作贴在「不应存在之物」上的封条。

examples.en: Slavery was described in the pamphlet as a moral abomination.
examples.cn: 小册子将奴隶制描述为道德上的可憎之制。

examples.en: The villagers held littering their holy grove in abomination.
examples.cn: 村民对在圣林中乱丢垃圾深恶痛绝。

examples.en: To the old architect, the concrete block was an abomination on the skyline.
examples.cn: 在老建筑师眼中，那座混凝土大楼是天际线上的一大败笔。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「饿泼米泥申」——剩饭泼得满地米和泥，众人齐声申斥：真可憎！

root: 拉丁语 abominatio：ab-（离开、拒斥）+ omen/omin-（预兆）+ -tio（名词后缀），本义「避拒凶兆之行为」，引申为「可憎之物、憎恶之情」。与 ominous 同根；与 denomination 等词仅拼写相近。

sensesIntro.en: The noun covers the hated thing, the feeling of loathing, and anything outrageously bad.
sensesIntro.cn: 名词涵盖被憎之物、憎恶之情，以及恶劣透顶之物。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a community turning its back together on one hateful thing.
core.cn: 核心意象：群体齐齐背对同一可憎之物。

branches.en: CONDEMNED PRACTICES: slavery, trafficking, and taboos the community refuses.
branches.cn: 受谴之行：奴隶制、贩卖、禁忌等群体拒斥之事。

branches.en: THE FEELING: loathing kept alive in the fixed older phrase.
branches.cn: 情感义：憎恶之感保留在旧式固定短语中。

branches.en: AESTHETIC DRIFT: tasteless buildings and works join the hated list.
branches.cn: 审美漂移：粗劣建筑与作品也进入可憎名单。

branches.en: OBJECT SENSE: both point at a thing, moral or aesthetic.
branches.cn: 对象义：两者都指向某物，或道德或审美。

branches.en: RELIGIOUS ROOT: scripture and church language kept the word strong.
branches.cn: 宗教根源：经文与教会语言维系了该词的力度。

intro.en: The word rides on ab- plus the omen root with noun and adjective endings.
intro.cn: 本词由 ab- 加 omen 词根，配名词与形容词后缀构成。

latinIntro.en: Latin keeps the omen family alive in English derivatives.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语使 omen 词族在英语派生词中延续。

definition_zh: 土著的；原住民的；土生的；原始的
definition_en: belonging to the people or species that were present in a place from the earliest times
core_image: 从土地最深处长出来的第一代人，脚与泥土连在一起
scene: 博物馆的展柜里摆着世代居住在河谷的人使用过的工具。The exhibition honours the aboriginal people of the river valley.
sceneCN: 这里 aboriginal 是「原住民的」（第 1 个义项：最早居住在某地的人群）；句意为展览致敬河谷的原住民。

derivatives.zh: 由本词去掉形容词后缀构成，义为「原住民；土著居民」
由形容词加副词后缀构成，义为「最初地；原初地」
由形容词加名词后缀构成，义为「原初性；本土性」

senses.title: Of a land's first peoples
senses.definition: belonging to the peoples who lived in a region before others arrived
senses.definitionCN: 属于在其他群体到来之前就居住于某地的人群
senses.example: The museum works with aboriginal communities.
senses.exampleCN: 博物馆与原住民社群合作。
senses.why: Latin ab origine means 'from the beginning'; the people who were there from the beginning are named by that phrase.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 ab origine 意为「从最初开始」；从一开始就在那里的人，正是由这个短语命名的。

senses.title: Native to a region
senses.definition: of a plant or animal, native to a place rather than introduced
senses.definitionCN: 指动植物原产于某地，而非外来引入
senses.example: The park protects several aboriginal species.
senses.exampleCN: 这座公园保护着几种本土物种。
senses.why: The 'from the beginning' idea applies to living things as well: a species that was there first is aboriginal to the land.
senses.whyCN: 「从最初开始」的观念也适用于生物：最早就在那里的物种，对这片土地而言就是土生的。

senses.title: Original and earliest
senses.definition: existing from the earliest period, before later changes
senses.definitionCN: 存在于最早时期、早于后来变化的
senses.example: The study traces aboriginal forms of the language.
senses.exampleCN: 这项研究追溯这种语言最早的形式。
senses.why: Anything that dates from the beginning can be called aboriginal, including ideas and language forms.
senses.whyCN: 任何始于最初的事物都可称为 aboriginal，包括观念与语言形式。

senses.title: Of Aboriginal Australia
senses.definition: relating to the Indigenous peoples of Australia
senses.definitionCN: 与澳大利亚原住民族群有关的
senses.example: She studies aboriginal art from the north.
senses.exampleCN: 她研究北部的原住民艺术。
senses.why: In Australian English the capitalized Aboriginal is the standard term for the continent's first peoples.
senses.whyCN: 在澳大利亚英语中，大写的 Aboriginal 是称呼该大陆最早居民的通用术语。

senses.title: Of a native culture
senses.definition: belonging to the culture of a place's first inhabitants
senses.definitionCN: 属于某地最早居民的文化
senses.example: The festival celebrates aboriginal traditions.
senses.exampleCN: 这个节日庆祝原住民传统。
senses.why: Culture is one of the things a first people carries, so the adjective naturally attaches to its songs, stories, and rites.
senses.whyCN: 文化是原住民族所承载的事物之一，因此这个形容词自然附着于他们的歌谣、故事与仪式。

senses.title: Growing in its native range
senses.definition: growing naturally in the area where it evolved
senses.definitionCN: 在它演化所在的地区自然生长
senses.example: These aboriginal grasses survive long droughts.
senses.exampleCN: 这些原生草种能挺过漫长干旱。
senses.why: A plant that has always grown in a region is a first inhabitant of that soil, and the word borrows the human image.
senses.whyCN: 一直在某地生长的植物，是那片土壤最早的居民，这个词借用了人的意象。

senses.title: Inherited from early ancestors
senses.definition: coming from the earliest ancestors of a group
senses.definitionCN: 来自某个群体最早的祖先
senses.example: The elders keep aboriginal knowledge of the seasons.
senses.exampleCN: 长者们保存着祖先传下的季节知识。
senses.why: Knowledge that passes from the first inhabitants is treated as part of the same inheritance.
senses.whyCN: 从最早居民传下来的知识，被视为同一份遗产的一部分。

senses.title: Untouched and original
senses.definition: describing a landscape or condition before outside change
senses.definitionCN: 形容在外部改变之前的地貌或状态
senses.example: The valley remains in its aboriginal state.
senses.exampleCN: 这个山谷仍保持原始状态。
senses.why: Landscapes untouched by later settlement are imagined as still standing at the beginning.
senses.whyCN: 未被后来定居改变的地貌，被想象成仍停在最初的样子。

intro.en: Aboriginal is built directly from a Latin phrase meaning 'from the beginning', and it preserves that phrase almost transparently.
intro.cn: aboriginal 直接由意为「从最初开始」的拉丁短语构成，几乎透明地保留了那个短语。

items.en: ab is a Latin preposition meaning 'from, away from'.
items.cn: ab 是拉丁语介词，意为「从、离开」。

items.en: origo meant 'a beginning, source, birth'; it also produced origin and original.
items.cn: origo 意为「开端、源头、出生」，也衍生出 origin 与 original。

items.en: The phrase ab origine, 'from the beginning', was used of peoples and things present from the first.
items.cn: 短语 ab origine 意为「从最初开始」，用于从一开始就存在的人群与事物。

items.en: The plural Aborigines named the first inhabitants of a region in Roman writing.
items.cn: 复数 Aborigines 在罗马文献中指某地最早的居民。

items.en: English aboriginal appears in the seventeenth century as an adjective for the earliest inhabitants.
items.cn: 英语 aboriginal 在十七世纪出现，作形容词指最早的居民。

items.en: The term spread to botany, geology, and Australian usage, where Aboriginal names the continent's first peoples.
items.cn: 这个术语扩展到植物学、地质学与澳大利亚用法；在那里，Aboriginal 指该大陆最早的居民。

note.en: The first group gathers the noun, adverb, and related origin words; the second gathers adjectives for what was there first.
note.cn: 第一组收名词、副词与相关的「起源」词；第二组收表示「最早就在那里」的形容词。

entries.definition: A member of the first people of a region; the noun behind the adjective.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「原住民、土著居民」，是形容词背后的名词形式。

entries.definition: The adverb meaning 'from the beginning or in the original state'.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「最初地、原初地」。

entries.definition: The quality of being original to a place.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「原初性、本土性」，指属于某地原初事物的性质。

entries.definition: The point where something begins; from the same Latin noun origo.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「起源」，来自同一个拉丁名词 origo。

entries.definition: Born or growing naturally in a particular place.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「土生土长的、原产的」，指在某地自然出生或生长。

entries.definition: Belonging to a place by birth or natural growth.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「本地的、天生的」，指因出生或自然生长而属于某地。

entries.definition: Existing from the start, before copies or changes.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「最初的、原来的」，指在复制或改变之前就存在。

entries.definition: Belonging to an early stage of development.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「原始的」，指属于发展的早期阶段。

entries.definition: Coming before all others in time or order.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「最早的、第一的」，在时间或顺序上先于其他。

normalIntro.en: The normal hooks work from the Latin phrase ab origine and the common policy collocations; the abstract hooks picture the first feet on the land.
normalIntro.cn: 常规记忆点来自拉丁短语 ab origine 与常见政策搭配；抽象记忆点想象最早踏上这片土地的脚。

normal.en: Aboriginal is literally ab origine, 'from the beginning'.
normal.cn: aboriginal 字面就是 ab origine，即「从最初开始」。

normal.en: Aboriginal people and aboriginal rights are standard public-policy phrases.
normal.cn: aboriginal people 与 aboriginal rights 是标准公共政策短语。

normal.en: Origin, original, and aboriginal all share the Latin noun origo.
normal.cn: origin、original 与 aboriginal 都共享拉丁名词 origo。

normal.en: In Australian English, Aboriginal with a capital letter names the continent's first peoples.
normal.cn: 在澳大利亚英语中，大写的 Aboriginal 指该大陆最早的居民。

normal.en: The adjective also works for plants and landscapes that were there first.
normal.cn: 这个形容词也适用于最早就在那里的植物与地貌。

abstract.en: Picture bare feet pressing into soil that no one else has walked on.
abstract.cn: 想象赤脚踩进无人走过的泥土。

abstract.en: Picture a seed already in the ground before any fence is built.
abstract.cn: 想象围栏尚未建起，种子早已在土里。

abstract.en: Picture a hand painting the same pattern that ancestors painted on rock.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手画出祖先曾画在岩石上的同一个图案。

examples.en: The law recognizes aboriginal land rights.
examples.cn: 法律承认原住民的土地权利。

examples.en: Several aboriginal languages are endangered.
examples.cn: 几种原住民语言濒临消亡。

examples.en: The valley still holds aboriginal forest.
examples.cn: 这个山谷仍保有原始森林。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿伯瑞金诺」——阿伯一出生就在这片土地上，脚底沾着最原始的泥。

root: 拉丁语 ab（从）+ origo（起源），短语 ab origine 意为「从最初开始」；核心义是「从一开始就在某地」

sensesIntro.en: The senses start with the first peoples, then extend to native species, earliest forms, Australian usage, culture, plants, inherited knowledge, and untouched landscapes.
sensesIntro.cn: 这些义项从最早的居民开始，扩展到本土物种、最早形式、澳大利亚用法、文化、植物、祖传知识与未开发的地貌。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the first feet standing on untouched ground
core.cn: 核心意象：最早踏上未动过的土地的双脚

branches.en: Human first peoples, including the capitalized Australian term.
branches.cn: 人类中最早的居民，包括澳大利亚的大写用法。

branches.en: Plants and animals native to a place from the start.
branches.cn: 从一开始就原产于某地的动植物。

branches.en: Earliest forms of language and knowledge passed down.
branches.cn: 传下来的最早语言形式与知识。

branches.en: The culture carried by a place's first inhabitants.
branches.cn: 某地最早居民所承载的文化。

branches.en: Landscapes still in their original, unchanged state.
branches.cn: 仍保持原初、未被改变的地貌。

intro.en: The word is transparently built from the Latin preposition ab and the noun origo, with the adjective ending -al.
intro.cn: 这个词由拉丁介词 ab、名词 origo 与形容词后缀 -al 透明地构成。

latinIntro.en: Latin origo and ab origine are the direct source of the English word, so the Latin entries record the phrase and its noun.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 origo 与短语 ab origine 是英语词的直接来源，因此拉丁条目记录这个短语及其名词。

derivatives.zh: 名词，义为「原住民；土著居民」
副词，义为「最初地；原初地」

definition_zh: 磨损；擦伤；磨掉表层
definition_en: to wear away or scrape off the surface of something by friction
core_image: 砂纸来回打磨，表层一点点消失
scene: 老师傅抓起工人的手看了看，皱起眉头说机器的毛边磨破了手套。Rough rocks abraded the paint on the hull.
sceneCN: 这里 abrade 是「磨掉表层」（第 1 个义项：粗石磨损船壳漆面）；句意为粗粝的岩石磨掉了船壳上的漆。

derivatives.zh: 由动词加名词后缀构成，义为「磨损处；擦伤」
由同一词根加形容词后缀构成，义为「磨损性的；（言行）粗鲁的」
由形容词加名词后缀构成，义为「磨损性；（性格）生硬」

senses.title: To wear away a surface by friction
senses.definition: to scrape or rub away the outer layer of a material or object
senses.definitionCN: 通过摩擦刮去或磨去材料、物体的表层
senses.example: Grit carried by the wind abraded the stone face of the monument.
senses.exampleCN: 风中夹带的砂粒磨蚀了纪念碑的石面。
senses.why: Latin ab- (off) plus radere (to scrape) keeps the image of something scraped away bit by bit.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 ab-（去掉）加 radere（刮），保留了「一点点刮掉」的意象。

senses.title: To scrape or wound the skin
senses.definition: to rub off or damage skin by rough contact, usually superficially
senses.definitionCN: 因粗糙接触而擦脱或损伤皮肤，通常只伤表层
senses.example: The rope abraded his palms as he slid down.
senses.exampleCN: 他往下滑时绳子磨破了手掌。
senses.why: Skin is just another surface, so the scraping image transfers from stone to flesh without change.
senses.whyCN: 皮肤不过是另一种表面，刮擦意象由石头原样转移到血肉。

senses.title: To be worn away by friction
senses.definition: intransitive use: to undergo wearing away through rubbing
senses.definitionCN: 不及物用法：因摩擦而逐渐被磨损
senses.example: Old inscriptions abrade quickly in sandy climates.
senses.exampleCN: 古老的铭文在多沙气候里很快被磨蚀。
senses.why: English verbs of action often flip to let the patient stand alone as subject.
senses.whyCN: 英语的动作动词常可翻转，让受事者单独充当主语。

intro.en: Abrade comes from Latin abradere, built on ab- 'off' and radere 'to scrape'; the same root gave rat and rodent-like words their scraping sense in razors and rays.
intro.cn: abrade 来自拉丁语 abradere，由 ab-「去掉」加 radere「刮」构成；同一词根还出现在 razor 等刮擦类词中。

items.en: A reconstructed root *ras- or *red- meant to scrape or scratch, generally regarded as the source of the Latin family.
items.cn: 重构词根 *ras-／*red- 义为刮、擦，一般认为是拉丁词族的来源。

items.en: Radere meant to scrape; rasp, erase, and razor descend from related forms.
items.cn: radere 义为刮；rasp、erase 与 razor 均出自相关词形。

items.en: Abradere added ab- 'off', making the scraping complete: to scrape away.
items.cn: abradere 加上 ab-「去掉」，使刮擦彻底：刮掉、磨掉。

items.en: The past participle abrasus fed later noun forms like abrasio.
items.cn: 过去分词 abrasus 衍生出 abrasio 等名词形式。

items.en: The verb entered English through learned or scientific writing, first for physical wear.
items.cn: 动词经学术与科学著作进入英语，最初指物理磨损。

items.en: Medicine and engineering keep the word for surface scraping, while abrasive carries a social metaphor.
items.cn: 医学与工程仍用其表「刮擦表面」，abrasive 则衍生出社交隐喻。

note.en: The first group is the scraping root family; the second lists wear-related verbs.
note.cn: 第一组为刮擦词根家族；第二组为表磨损的动词。

entries.definition: the scraped spot or the process of wearing away.
entries.definitionCN: 磨损处或磨损过程。

entries.definition: scraping hard, or figuratively harsh in manner.
entries.definitionCN: 磨损性的；引申指言语态度粗鲁。

entries.definition: to rub out writing; from e- plus the same scraping root.
entries.definitionCN: 擦除字迹；由 e- 加同一刮擦词根构成。

entries.definition: to repeal a law; only ab- is shared, the root is different.
entries.definitionCN: 废除法律；仅共享 ab- 前缀，词根不同。

entries.definition: to crush or wear down by friction, usually with force.
entries.definitionCN: 以摩擦碾碎或磨耗，通常用力较大。

entries.definition: to rub and make sore, especially skin.
entries.definitionCN: 摩擦致痛，尤指皮肤。

entries.definition: to eat away chemically rather than by friction.
entries.definitionCN: 以化学方式侵蚀，而非摩擦。

entries.definition: to drag something rough across a surface.
entries.definitionCN: 用粗糙物在表面拖刮。

entries.definition: to make a surface smooth and shiny; the aim is opposite to abrade.
entries.definitionCN: 使表面光滑发亮；目的与 abrade 相反。

normalIntro.en: Break the word into ab- plus the scrape root.
normalIntro.cn: 把单词拆成 ab- 加刮擦词根来记。

normal.en: ab- = off; rad- = scrape; so scrape off.
normal.cn: ab- = 去掉；rad- = 刮；合起来即「刮掉」。

normal.en: Family: eraser erases by the same scraping idea.
normal.cn: 词族：eraser 靠同一「刮擦」观念擦字。

normal.en: razor and raze share the family image of shaving away.
normal.cn: razor 与 raze 同属「刮平、剃去」意象家族。

normal.en: -e verb ending: abrade → abraded → abrasion.
normal.cn: 动词以 -e 结尾：abrade → abraded → abrasion。

normal.en: Think sandpaper: its whole job is to abrade.
normal.cn: 想想砂纸：其全部职责就是磨蚀。

abstract.en: Hear the dry hiss of sandpaper on wood.
abstract.cn: 听砂纸打磨木头时干涩的沙沙声。

abstract.en: Feel rope fiber biting into a palm.
abstract.cn: 体会绳索纤维咬进掌心的感觉。

abstract.en: See a stone inscription slowly going faint.
abstract.cn: 看石碑铭文一点点变淡。

examples.en: Ceaseless tides abrade the base of the cliffs.
examples.cn: 不息的潮水磨蚀着崖基。

examples.en: Workers abraded the glossy layer before repainting the wall.
examples.cn: 工人们先把光亮层磨掉，再给墙重新刷漆。

examples.en: Long hikes had abraded the toes of his boots thin.
examples.cn: 长途跋涉把他的靴头磨薄了。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「我别锐的」——刀别太锐，来回一磨就磨损了。

root: 拉丁语 abradere：ab-（去掉）+ radere（刮、擦）。印欧词根一般认为重构为 *ras-/*red-「刮擦」，同族词含 erase、razor、rasp 等。动词经十七世纪学术英语定型，核心义始终是「以摩擦去掉表层」。

sensesIntro.en: One image of scraping spreads to materials, skin, and the wearing-away process itself.
sensesIntro.cn: 「刮擦」一个意象延伸到材料、皮肤与磨损过程本身。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: sandpaper dragging a surface thinner stroke by stroke.
core.cn: 核心意象：砂纸一下一下把表面拖磨变薄。

branches.en: MATERIALS: wind, grit, and tools wear stone, paint, and metal.
branches.cn: 材料：风、砂粒与工具磨损石、漆、金属。

branches.en: BODY: ropes and rough cloth scrape the skin.
branches.cn: 身体：绳索与粗布擦伤皮肤。

branches.en: PATIENT SUBJECT: the worn thing itself takes the verb.
branches.cn: 受事主语：被磨损之物自身作主语。

branches.en: PROCESS VIEW: abrade names the slow mechanical loss of surface.
branches.cn: 过程视角：abrade 指表层缓慢的机械性损耗。

branches.en: MEDICINE: abrasion grades keep the scraping image in clinical use.
branches.cn: 医学：擦伤分级使刮擦意象进入临床用语。

intro.en: The scrape root rad- builds a wide family of rubbing words.
intro.cn: 刮擦词根 rad- 构建了一个庞大的摩擦词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin relatives keep scraping visible in English.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁同族词让「刮擦」在英语中处处可见。

items.meaning: to scrape or level to the ground
items.example: raze a building to the ground

derivatives.zh: 名词，义为「磨损；擦伤处」
形容词，义为「磨损性的；粗鲁的」

definition_zh: 磨损；磨蚀；擦伤处
definition_en: the act of wearing away by friction, or the scraped spot itself
core_image: 被砂纸磨出的一道道浅痕
scene: 工长蹲下来摸了摸护栏，说这里的锈斑全是砂粒磨出来的。Road grit had left deep abrasions on the railing.
sceneCN: 这里 abrasion 是「磨损处」（第 1 个义项：砂粒在护栏上磨出的伤痕）；句意为路面的砂粒在护栏上磨出了深深的痕迹。

derivatives.zh: 由同一词干加动词后缀回构，义为「磨损；擦伤」
由同词干加形容词后缀构成，义为「磨损性的；（磨料）」

senses.title: A scraped or worn spot
senses.definition: a place on skin or material where the surface has been scraped off
senses.definitionCN: 皮肤或材料表面被磨脱、擦破之处
senses.example: The climber treated the abrasions on his knees at camp.
senses.exampleCN: 登山者在营地处理膝盖上的擦伤。
senses.why: The participle abrasus names what has been scraped; the noun keeps the visible mark.
senses.whyCN: 分词 abrasus 指「被刮过的」，名词保留了可见的伤痕。

senses.title: The process of wearing away
senses.definition: the gradual removal of surface material by rubbing or grinding
senses.definitionCN: 因摩擦或研磨而逐渐去除表层材料的过程
senses.example: Desert wind causes slow abrasion of sandstone formations.
senses.exampleCN: 沙漠之风使砂岩地貌慢慢受到磨蚀。
senses.why: The scraped spot implies an ongoing action; engineering and geology keep the process sense.
senses.whyCN: 伤痕暗示持续的动作；工程与地质保留了这一过程义。

senses.title: Scrapping or rubbing off deliberately
senses.definition: the act of roughening or cleaning a surface by abrasion before bonding or painting
senses.definitionCN: 在粘合或喷涂前以打磨使表面粗糙或洁净
senses.example: Light abrasion of the panel helps the primer stick.
senses.exampleCN: 对板材轻度打磨有助于底漆附着。
senses.why: What nature does slowly, a workshop can do on purpose; the action sense becomes a technique.
senses.whyCN: 自然界缓慢之事，车间可为技艺；磨蚀义转为一种工艺。

intro.en: Abrasion comes from Latin abrasio, formed on the participle abrasus of abradere 'to scrape off', from ab- 'off' and radere 'to scrape'.
intro.cn: abrasion 来自拉丁语 abrasio，由 abradere「刮掉」的过去分词 abrasus 构成，ab-「去掉」加 radere「刮」。

items.en: A reconstructed root *ras- or *red- meant to scrape or scratch, generally regarded as the source of the family.
items.cn: 重构词根 *ras-／*red- 义为刮、擦，一般认为即该词族之源。

items.en: Radere meant to scrape; razor, erase, and rasp descend from related forms.
items.cn: radere 义为刮；razor、erase 与 rasp 出自相关词形。

items.en: Abradere combined ab- with the root: to scrape away completely.
items.cn: abradere 把 ab- 与词根结合：彻底刮掉。

items.en: Abrasio named both the scraping act and the scraped result.
items.cn: abrasio 兼指刮擦行为与刮痕结果。

items.en: The noun entered English in medical texts for skin scrapes before engineering widened it.
items.cn: 名词先随医学文本进入英语，指皮肤擦伤，后经工程学扩展。

items.en: Today it spans first aid, materials testing, and geology, always naming friction loss.
items.cn: 如今横跨急救、材料测试与地质学，始终指摩擦造成的损耗。

note.en: The first group is the scraping root family; the second lists wear and damage nouns.
note.cn: 第一组为刮擦词根家族；第二组为磨损与损伤类名词。

entries.definition: to wear away a surface by friction.
entries.definitionCN: 以摩擦磨掉表层。

entries.definition: scraping hard, or figuratively harsh in manner.
entries.definitionCN: 磨损性的；引申指言语粗鲁。

entries.definition: to rub out writing, from the same scraping root.
entries.definitionCN: 擦除字迹，同享刮擦词根。

entries.definition: the quality of scraping or of being harsh.
entries.definitionCN: 磨损性；粗鲁生硬。

entries.definition: self-restraint from indulgence; looks close but has a different root.
entries.definitionCN: 节制、戒绝；拼写相近但词根不同。

entries.definition: a shallow scrape, especially on skin.
entries.definitionCN: 浅表擦伤，尤指皮肤。

examples.cn: 报告指出刹车线护套存在磨损。

examples.en: Glacial abrasion polished the valley walls smooth.

sensesIntro.en: One scraped surface gives a visible mark, an ongoing process, and a workshop technique.
sensesIntro.cn: 「被刮的表面」分出可见伤痕、持续过程与工艺手法三枝。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: shallow streaks where a surface has been rubbed thin.
core.cn: 核心意象：表面被磨薄处留下的一道道浅痕。

branches.en: WOUNDS: knees and palms show shallow abrasions.
branches.cn: 伤口：膝、掌常见浅表擦伤。

branches.en: GEOLOGY AND ENGINEERING: wind, grit, and glaciers wear rock and parts.
branches.cn: 地质与工程：风、砂粒与冰川磨损岩石与部件。

branches.en: WORKSHOP: light abrasion prepares surfaces for paint.

definition_zh: 删节；节略；缩短；剥夺（权利）
definition_en: to make a text, speech, or period shorter, or to cut down a right or freedom
core_image: 一把红笔在厚书上划掉整段，书页变薄
scene: 出版社的编辑桌上堆着一部厚厚的长篇小说，红笔已经划掉了几十页。The publisher abridged the long novel for young readers.
sceneCN: 这里 abridge 是「删节文字作品」（第 1 个义项：删去部分内容使篇幅变短）；句意为出版社为年轻读者删节了这部长篇小说。

pos.zh: 及物动词：删节；节略；缩短；剥夺；限制

senses.title: To shorten a text by cutting parts
senses.definition: to shorten a book, article, or other text by removing parts of it
senses.definitionCN: 删去书、文章或其他文本的部分内容，使其变短
senses.example: The publisher abridged the long novel for young readers.
senses.exampleCN: 出版社为年轻读者删节了这部长篇小说。
senses.why: breviare, from brevis 'short', is the root; cutting a text is the plainest way to make it short.
senses.whyCN: 词根 breviare 出自 brevis「短」；把文本删掉一部分，正是让它变短最直白的方式。

senses.title: To produce a shortened edition
senses.definition: to prepare a shorter version of a work for publication or performance
senses.definitionCN: 为出版或演出准备一个篇幅更短的版本
senses.example: The play was abridged for a single evening.
senses.exampleCN: 这个剧本被压缩成一场晚会能演完的版本。
senses.why: Here the cutting serves a fixed frame: the edition must fit a page count or a stage time.
senses.whyCN: 这里的删减服务于一个固定框架：版本必须装进规定的页数或演出时长。

senses.title: To shorten a speech or statement
senses.definition: to make a speech, report, or statement shorter
senses.definitionCN: 使讲话、报告或陈述变得更短
senses.example: She abridged her remarks to ten minutes.
senses.exampleCN: 她把发言压缩到十分钟。
senses.why: Spoken words are cut the same way written ones are: the material is shortened before delivery.
senses.whyCN: 口头的话语与书面文字一样被剪短：材料在说出之前就被压缩。

senses.title: To shorten a period of time
senses.definition: to make a period or process shorter in duration
senses.definitionCN: 使一段时间或过程持续得更短
senses.example: The new route abridges the journey by an hour.
senses.exampleCN: 新路线把行程缩短了一个小时。
senses.why: If a stretch of time is a length, it can be cut like a page; the metaphor is one of measured extent.
senses.whyCN: 如果把一段时间看作一段长度，它就能像书页一样被剪短；这个比喻建立在「可量的长度」上。

senses.title: To shorten a distance or way
senses.definition: to make a distance or route shorter, an older sense still found in formal prose
senses.definitionCN: 使距离或路线变短，这一较旧的义项仍见于正式书面语
senses.example: A tunnel would abridge the road between the two towns.
senses.exampleCN: 一条隧道会缩短两镇之间的路程。
senses.why: A road is a line on the ground; cutting it short is the spatial version of the same shortening.
senses.whyCN: 道路是地面上的一条线；把它截短，是同一个「缩短」在空间上的版本。

senses.title: To condense to the essential points
senses.definition: to reduce material to its essential points without losing the main sense
senses.definitionCN: 把材料压缩到要点，同时不丢失主要意思
senses.example: The summary abridges three chapters into one page.
senses.exampleCN: 这份摘要把三章内容压缩成一页。
senses.why: Shortening well is not random deletion: what remains must still carry the whole, so the cut is a condensation.
senses.whyCN: 好的删节不是随意删除：留下来的部分仍要承载整体，所以这种剪切是一种浓缩。

senses.title: To deprive someone of a right
senses.definition: in law, to deprive a person of a right, privilege, or benefit
senses.definitionCN: 法律用语，指剥夺某人的权利、特权或利益
senses.example: The old statute abridged the rights of tenants.
senses.exampleCN: 那条旧法令剥夺了租户的权利。
senses.why: A right is treated as something a person holds; cutting it off leaves the holder with less than before.
senses.whyCN: 权利被当作人手里握有的东西；把它切掉，持有人就比原来少了。

senses.title: To limit freedom or power
senses.definition: to restrict or cut down a freedom, power, or authority
senses.definitionCN: 限制或削减自由、权力或权威
senses.example: No law may abridge freedom of speech.
senses.exampleCN: 任何法律都不得限制言论自由。
senses.why: The legal sense widens from a single right to any freedom: whatever is cut down is abridged.
senses.whyCN: 法律义从单项权利扩展到任何自由：凡是被削减的，就是被 abridge。

intro.en: Abridge came through Old French from a Late Latin verb built on the adjective brevis, 'short'.
intro.cn: abridge 经古法语来自一个晚期拉丁动词，其词根是形容词 brevis「短的」。

items.en: brevis meant short or brief, and it is the source of English brief and brevity.
items.cn: brevis 意为「短的、简短的」，是英语 brief 与 brevity 的来源。

items.en: breviare, 'to shorten', was formed from brevis; with ad- it became abbreviare.
items.cn: breviare「缩短」由 brevis 构成；加上 ad- 后成为 abbreviare。

items.en: Late Latin abbreviare, 'to shorten', passed into Old French as abregier.
items.cn: 晚期拉丁语 abbreviare「缩短」传入古法语，成为 abregier。

items.en: Old French abregier carried the word into Middle English as abreggen.
items.cn: 古法语 abregier 把这个词带入中古英语，作 abreggen。

items.en: English abridge is recorded from the fourteenth century; the exact first date is uncertain.
items.cn: 英语 abridge 自十四世纪起有记录；确切首见年代不确定。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the brevity family and the longer Latin stem; the near-meaning group gathers verbs of cutting and condensing.
note.cn: 形近组收 brevity 词族与较长的拉丁词干；近义组收表示剪切与压缩的动词。

entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「删节；节略本」，由 abridge 加 -ment 构成。

entries.definition: Shortened by having parts removed, of a text or edition.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「删节过的」，由 abridge 加 -ed 构成。

entries.definition: Complete, with nothing removed; the opposite of abridged.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「未删节的、完整的」，由 un- 加 abridged 构成。

entries.definition: To shorten a word, phrase, or text, from the same Latin brevis.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「缩写、缩短」，与 abridge 同出拉丁语 brevis「短」。

entries.definition: Shortness of speech or writing, from Latin brevitas.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「简短、简洁」，同样出自 brevis，但只指风格上的短。

entries.definition: To make something shorter in length, time, or duration; the most general word.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「使变短」，用于长度、时间或篇幅，是最一般的说法。

entries.definition: To make a text or substance denser by reducing what is in it.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「压缩、浓缩」，强调减少内容或体积后更紧凑。

entries.definition: To cut off the end of something, especially in computing or geometry.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「截断、截短」，多用于计算机或几何，强调去掉末端。

entries.definition: To reduce or cut short a right, spending, or an activity.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「削减、缩短」，多用于权利、开支或活动，语气正式。

entries.definition: To remove part of a text, film, or budget; the everyday verb behind abridge.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「删剪、削减」，是 abridge 背后最日常的说法。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real Latin root brevis and the phrases the word appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子使用真实的拉丁词根 brevis，以及这个词出现的搭配。

normal.en: brevis is Latin for short: abridge is to make short.
normal.cn: brevis 是拉丁语的「短」：abridge 就是使变短。

normal.en: abbreviate and brevity come from the same brevis, so the family shares one idea.
normal.cn: abbreviate 与 brevity 同出 brevis，整个词族共享一个「短」的念头。

normal.en: An abridged edition cuts a text; an unabridged one keeps every word.
normal.cn: abridged edition 删节文本；unabridged 版本则一字不减。

normal.en: abridgement is the noun for both the act and the shortened version.
normal.cn: abridgement 既是「删节」这个动作，也指删节后的版本。

normal.en: In law, to abridge a right is to cut it short.
normal.cn: 在法律里，abridge a right 就是把一项权利切短。

abstract.en: Picture a thick book with a pair of scissors laid beside it: the cut pages are what disappear.
abstract.cn: 想象一本厚书旁边放着一把剪刀：消失的正是被剪下的书页。

abstract.en: The same scissors can cut a speech, a journey, a timetable or a legal right.
abstract.cn: 同一把剪刀可以剪短讲话、旅程、时间表，也可以剪掉一项法律权利。

abstract.en: Good abridging keeps the shape of the whole while removing what can be spared.
abstract.cn: 好的删节保留整体的形状，只去掉可以省去的部分。

examples.en: The editors abridged the report to four pages.
examples.cn: 编辑把报告删节到四页。

examples.en: This is the abridged edition, not the full text.
examples.cn: 这是节略本，不是全文。

examples.en: The court ruled that the new rule abridged free speech.
examples.cn: 法院裁定新规定限制了言论自由。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses all shorten something: a text, an edition, a speech, a period, a route, a summary, a right, or a freedom.

branches.en: THE TEXT: a book or article loses the parts that can be spared.
branches.cn: 文本线：书或文章失去那些可以省去的部分。

branches.en: THE EDITION: a shorter version is made for a fixed frame, keeping the essential points.
branches.cn: 版本线：为固定框架制作较短的版本，同时保留要点。

branches.en: THE SPEECH: spoken words are cut short before they are delivered.
branches.cn: 讲话线：口头内容在说出之前就被压缩。

branches.en: THE MEASURE: a period of time or a route is shortened as if it were a length.
branches.cn: 度量线：一段时间或一条路线像长度一样被截短。

branches.en: THE RIGHT: law cuts down a right, a freedom, or a power.
branches.cn: 权利线：法律削减一项权利、自由或权力。

definition_zh: 废除；废止（法律、协议、惯例）
definition_en: to repeal or abolish a law, agreement, or custom formally
core_image: 一纸判词把旧条文划掉作废
scene: 议长敲下木槌，宣布那条过时的税法从今天起不再有效。The new government abrogated the decades-old treaty.
sceneCN: 这里 abrogate 是「废除」（第 1 个义项：新政府废除旧条约）；句意为新政府废除了那项数十年之久的条约。

derivatives.zh: 由动词加名词后缀构成，义为「废除；废止」
由动词加形容词后缀构成，义为「有废除权的；废止性的」

senses.title: To repeal a law or agreement formally
senses.definition: to annul or repeal a law, treaty, or contract by formal authority
senses.definitionCN: 由正式权力机关废止或撤销法律、条约或合同
senses.example: Parliament voted to abrogate the emergency decree.
senses.exampleCN: 议会表决废除了那项紧急法令。
senses.why: Latin ab- (away) plus rogare (to propose a law) means to call a law away, cancelling its force.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 ab-（离去）加 rogare（提出法案），义为把法律「召离」，使其失效。

senses.title: To end a practice or obligation
senses.definition: to put an end to an established custom or duty as if repealing it
senses.definitionCN: 像废止法条一样终结既有的惯例或义务
senses.example: The reform abrogated centuries of patronage appointments.
senses.exampleCN: 改革终结了延续数百年的恩惠任命。
senses.why: What custom treated as binding is treated as if it were written law, so the repeal verb extends to it.
senses.whyCN: 惯例本有约束力，被当作成文法对待，废除动词随之延伸至惯例。

intro.en: Abrogate comes from Latin abrogatus, past participle of abrogare 'to repeal', from ab- 'away' and rogare 'to propose a law'.
intro.cn: abrogate 来自拉丁语 abrogatus，是 abrogare「废除」的过去分词，由 ab-「离去」加 rogare「提出法案」构成。

items.en: Rogare meant to ask formally, especially to ask the people to accept a law.
items.cn: rogare 义为正式请求，尤指请求民众接受一项法律。

items.en: In Roman usage, abrogare was the technical term for repealing a statute through vote.
items.cn: 在罗马用法中，abrogare 是经表决废止法规的术语。

items.en: Derogare, by contrast, meant only to subtract part of a law; the pair kept distinct legal senses.
items.cn: 与之相对，derogare 只指削减法律的某部分；两者在法律语中分工明确。

items.en: Subrogare meant to put another law in the place of the repealed one.
items.cn: subrogare 指以另一法条取代被废者。

items.en: The word entered English legal and theological writing with the full Roman sense.
items.cn: 十六世纪该词带着完整的罗马法意义进入英语法律与神学著作。

items.en: It stays formal, reserved for laws, treaties, and solemn institutional acts.
items.cn: 如今仍属正式用语，限于法律、条约与庄严的机构行为。

note.en: The first group gathers the rogare family; the second lists repeal-related verbs.
note.cn: 第一组为 rogare 词族；第二组为表废除的动词。

entries.definition: the act of repealing or the repealed state.
entries.definitionCN: 废除行为或被废状态。

entries.definition: to claim without right; shares the rogare root but means seizing, not repealing.
entries.definitionCN: 僭取；同享 rogare 词根，但义为擅夺而非废除。

entries.definition: to detract from or partially repeal; Roman law partner of abrogate.
entries.definitionCN: 贬损或部分废止；罗马法中与 abrogate 相对。

entries.definition: to question formally; the asking root without the repealing sense.
entries.definitionCN: 正式质询；同根但只有「问」义。

entries.definition: to give up a throne or duty; looks close but comes from dicere, not rogare.
entries.definitionCN: 放弃王位或职责；形近但词根是 dicere 而非 rogare。

entries.definition: to withdraw a law officially; the everyday legal partner.
entries.definitionCN: 正式撤回法律；日常法律对应词。

entries.definition: to declare something void from the start, as with a marriage.
entries.definitionCN: 宣告自始无效，如宣告婚姻无效。

entries.definition: to cancel a contract or order retroactively.
entries.definitionCN: 追溯性地取消合同或命令。

entries.definition: to confirm formally; the opposite institutional move.
entries.definitionCN: 正式批准；机构行为上的反向操作。

entries.definition: to put a rule back into force after repeal.
entries.definitionCN: 废除后恢复某规则的效力。

normalIntro.en: Use the rogare root and the legal family.
normalIntro.cn: 利用 rogare 词根与法律词族记忆。

normal.en: ab- away + rogare ask-a-law = call the law away.
normal.cn: ab- 离去 + rogare 立法之问 = 把法律召离作废。

normal.en: interrogate asks questions; abrogate asks laws away.
normal.cn: interrogate 问问题，abrogate 把法律问走。

normal.en: Derogate subtracts a part; abrogate ends the whole.
normal.cn: derogate 削去一部，abrogate 废除全部。

normal.en: arrogate is the sound twin, but it seizes instead.
normal.cn: arrogate 是音形孪生词，但义为擅夺。

normal.en: -ation noun: abrogation appears in legal writing.
normal.cn: -ation 名词：abrogation 常见于法律文书。

abstract.en: Hear the gavel striking a law out of existence.
abstract.cn: 听法槌一击，把法律敲得灰飞烟灭。

abstract.en: See a treaty torn in two on a green table.
abstract.cn: 看一条约在绿呢桌上被撕成两半。

abstract.en: Feel the weight lift when an old rule dies.
abstract.cn: 体会旧规失效时如释重负之感。

examples.en: The court ruled that the agency could not abrogate the statute on its own.
examples.cn: 法院裁定该机构无权自行废止该法规。

examples.en: The two states agreed to abrogate their border accord peacefully.
examples.cn: 两国同意和平废除边界协定。

examples.en: Critics feared the council would abrogate long-standing traditions overnight.
examples.cn: 批评者担心委员会会一夜之间废除既有传统。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿波罗规特」——像阿波罗神谕那样特别正式地把规矩废掉。

root: 拉丁语 abrogare：ab-（离去）+ rogare（正式提请、立法之问）。在罗马法中特指经表决废止整部法规，与 derogare（部分削减）、subrogare（以新代旧）分工。十六世纪经学术英语进入法律与神学语域，至今保持正式色彩。

sensesIntro.en: The verb moves from repealing formal instruments to ending binding customs.
sensesIntro.cn: 动词由废止正式文书延伸到终结有约束力的惯例。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a gavel stroke cancelling a written rule.
core.cn: 核心意象：法槌一击，成文规则当场作废。

branches.en: INSTRUMENTS: treaties, decrees, and statutes die by formal act.
branches.cn: 文书：条约、法令与法规经正式行为废止。

branches.en: CUSTOMS: patronage and old habits treated as implicit law.
branches.cn: 惯例：恩惠任命与旧习被视作不成文之法。

branches.en: AUTHORITY REQUIRED: only a competent body can abrogate.
branches.cn: 须有权威：唯有适格机构可行废除。

branches.en: WHOLENESS: unlike derogate, the repeal is complete.
branches.cn: 整体性：与 derogate 不同，废除是彻底的。

branches.en: FORMAL REGISTER: everyday speech prefers repeal or scrap.
branches.cn: 正式语域：日常口语更常说 repeal 或 scrap。

intro.en: Rogare, the asking-and-law-making root, seeds many formal English verbs.
intro.cn: rogare 这一「请问、立法」词根衍生出多个正式英语动词。

latinIntro.en: Latin legal verbs survive in English institutional language.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁法律动词保留在英语制度性语言中。

latinEntries.meaning: to repeal a statute by vote

definition_zh: 突然的；唐突的；生硬的；（地形）陡峭的
definition_en: sudden and unexpected, or rudely short in manner
core_image: 话说到一半被生生打断的陡然一截
scene: 他刚举手要提问，灯忽然全灭了，全场愣在原地。The meeting came to an abrupt end when the alarm went off.
sceneCN: 这里 abrupt 是「突然的」（第 1 个义项：会议骤然中断）；句意为警报一响，会议戛然而止。

derivatives.zh: 由形容词加副词后缀构成，义为「突然地；生硬地」
由形容词加名词后缀构成，义为「突然；生硬」
同根词，义为「破裂」，共享「断裂」词根

senses.title: Sudden and unexpected
senses.definition: happening quickly without warning, cutting off what went before
senses.definitionCN: 毫无预兆地迅速发生，中断先前进程
senses.example: Their journey ended in an abrupt stop at the landslide.
senses.exampleCN: 山体滑坡让他们的旅程戛然而止。
senses.why: Latin rumpere means to break; something abrupt is, literally, broken off.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 rumpere 义为断裂；abrupt 字面即「被折断的」。

senses.title: Rudely brief in speech or manner
senses.definition: speaking or behaving in a curt, unfriendly, clipped way
senses.definitionCN: 言谈举止简短生硬、不客气
senses.example: Tired from the night shift, he gave an abrupt no to the reporter.
senses.exampleCN: 夜班后的他生硬地拒绝了记者。
senses.why: Conversation broken off mid-flow feels like the broken-off stone: short and sheer.
senses.whyCN: 话被中途打断，正如被折断的石头：又短又陡。

senses.title: Steep, with a sharp rise
senses.definition: of ground or slopes, rising sharply at a near-vertical angle
senses.definitionCN: 指地势或坡面近乎垂直地陡然升高
senses.example: An abrupt cliff guarded the northern shore.
senses.exampleCN: 陡峭的悬崖护卫着北岸。
senses.why: The land itself looks broken: the level ends and the rock jumps up.
senses.whyCN: 地形本身如同断裂：平地到此为止，岩石陡然拔起。

intro.en: Abrupt comes from Latin abruptus, past participle of abrumpere 'to break off', from ab- 'away' and rumpere 'to break'.
intro.cn: abrupt 来自拉丁语 abruptus，是 abrumpere「折断」的过去分词，由 ab-「离去」加 rumpere「断裂」构成。

items.en: A reconstructed root *reup- or *reub- meant to snatch or break, generally regarded as the source of rumpere.
items.cn: 重构词根 *reup-／*reub- 义为夺、断，一般认为是 rumpere 的来源。

items.en: Rumpere meant to break, burst, or smash; rupture and corrupt share it.
items.cn: rumpere 义为打断、爆裂；rupture 与 corrupt 同根。

items.en: Abrumpere added ab-: to break something off short.
items.cn: abrumpere 加 ab-：把某物齐齐折断。

items.en: Abruptus described broken-off things, chiefly steep, sheer ground.
items.cn: abruptus 描述被折断之物，主要指陡峭地形。

items.en: A closeness of style between sharp turns of thought and the Latin word encouraged later transferred senses.
items.cn: 思路陡转与该拉丁词之间风格相近，促成后来的引申义。

items.en: English took abrupt for steep ground first, then for sudden events and curt manners.
items.cn: 英语先取「陡峭」义，后扩展至事件骤发与态度生硬。

note.en: The first group is the rumpere breaking family; the second lists suddenness words.
note.cn: 第一组为 rumpere 断裂词族；第二组为表「突然」的词。

entries.definition: in a sudden or curt way.
entries.definitionCN: 突然地；生硬地。

entries.definition: a breaking or burst, medical or mechanical.
entries.definitionCN: 破裂、爆裂，医学或机械用语。

entries.definition: to break out violently, as a volcano.
entries.definitionCN: 爆发，如火山喷发。

entries.definition: to break into a flow of speech or action.
entries.definitionCN: 打断言语或行动。

entries.definition: morally broken or rotten; same root, different prefix.
entries.definitionCN: 腐败的；同根不同前缀。

entries.definition: to repeal a law; shares ab- only.
entries.definitionCN: 废除法律；仅共享 ab-。

entries.definition: happening quickly, without the broken-off image.
entries.definitionCN: 迅速发生，无「折断」意象。

entries.definition: rudely brief in speech, only about manner.
entries.definitionCN: 言辞生硬简短，仅指态度。

entries.definition: rising sharply, only about slope.
entries.definitionCN: 陡峭的，仅指坡度。

entries.definition: changing step by step; the opposite of abrupt.
entries.definitionCN: 逐步的；abrupt 之反义。

normalIntro.en: Hold the broken-off image and the rupture family.
normalIntro.cn: 抓住「折断」意象与 rupture 词族。

normal.en: ab- away + rupt break = broken off.
normal.cn: ab- 离去 + rupt 断裂 = 被折断。

normal.en: interrupt, erupt, rupture, corrupt — one root, many breaks.
normal.cn: interrupt、erupt、rupture、corrupt——同根多断。

normal.en: Three faces: sudden events, curt speech, steep slopes.
normal.cn: 三副面孔：事之骤、言之硬、地之陡。

normal.en: Fixed phrase: come to an abrupt end.
normal.cn: 固定短语：come to an abrupt end。

normal.en: Opposite: gradual change, smooth slope, polite reply.
normal.cn: 反义：渐变、缓坡、客气回答。

abstract.en: Hear a record scratch stop the music dead.
abstract.cn: 听唱片刮擦声让音乐戛然而止。

abstract.en: See a cliff face drop straight into the sea.
abstract.cn: 看崖壁直插入海。

abstract.en: Feel a one-word answer end a friendly talk.
abstract.cn: 体会一个字的回答终结友好交谈。

examples.en: The weather took an abrupt turn toward freezing rain.
examples.cn: 天气骤变，转为冻雨。

examples.en: His abrupt tone made the interns hesitant to ask questions.
examples.cn: 他生硬的语气让实习生不敢提问。

examples.en: Hikers choose the gradual trail to avoid the abrupt western face.
examples.cn: 远足者选择缓路，避开西侧的陡崖。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「我不让他普讲」——他突然打断，不让人把话讲完。

root: 拉丁语 abrumpere：ab-（离去）+ rumpere（断裂，印欧词根一般认为重构为 *reup-「夺、断」）。过去分词 abruptus 本义「被折断的」，先指陡峭地形，十六世纪入英语后延伸至事件骤发与言语生硬。同根词 rupture、erupt、interrupt、corrupt。

sensesIntro.en: One broken-off image branches into sudden events, curt manners, and sheer slopes.
sensesIntro.cn: 「折断」一个意象分出骤变、生硬与陡峭三枝。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: something continuous snapped clean in two.
core.cn: 核心意象：连续之物被齐齐折成两截。

branches.en: EVENTS: journeys, meetings, weather end without warning.
branches.cn: 事件：旅程、会议、天气骤然中断。

branches.en: MANNER: clipped answers break the flow of talk.
branches.cn: 态度：生硬简答截断话流。

branches.en: LAND: slopes jump where level ground ends.
branches.cn: 地形：平地尽处陡然拔起。

branches.en: CUTTING: both senses stress what was stopped mid-course.
branches.cn: 截断：两义都强调中途被止。

branches.en: OPPOSITE POLE: gradual change and gentle grades.
branches.cn: 反义一端：渐变与缓坡。

intro.en: The rumpere root powers a whole family of breaking words.
intro.cn: rumpere 词根撑起整个「断裂」词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin compounds of rumpere mark what breaks and how.
latinIntro.cn: rumpere 的拉丁复合词标示断裂的方式与方向。

definition_zh: 潜逃；携款潜逃；悄悄溜走以躲避
definition_en: to leave hurriedly and secretly to avoid detection or arrest
core_image: 抱着东西从后门趁夜溜走
scene: 出纳的桌上还摊着账本，人却不见了，谁也没听见门响。The cashier absconded with the week's takings.
sceneCN: 这里 abscond 是「携款潜逃」（第 2 个义项：卷走现款逃走）；句意为出纳带着本周的营业款潜逃了。

derivatives.zh: 由动词加名词后缀构成，义为「潜逃者」
由动词加名词后缀构成的罕见名词，义为「潜逃行为」
同根形容词，义为「隐秘的、与世隔绝的」，与潜逃义相关但不同词

senses.title: To hide oneself away from authority
senses.definition: to withdraw into hiding so that police, creditors, or guardians cannot find one
senses.definitionCN: 躲藏起来，使警察、债主或监护人无法找到
senses.example: The debtor absconded to a remote village until the statute ran out.
senses.exampleCN: 债务人躲到偏僻村庄，直到诉讼时效届满。
senses.why: Latin abscondere means to stow away out of sight; the verb keeps that image of vanishing into concealment.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 abscondere 义为藏起来不见踪影，动词保留了「隐入藏匿处」的意象。

senses.title: To run off with something taken
senses.definition: to flee secretly taking money, goods, or evidence with one
senses.definitionCN: 带着钱款、财物或证据秘密逃走
senses.example: Two clerks absconded with the payroll before dawn.
senses.exampleCN: 两名职员天亮前卷走工资款逃走了。
senses.why: One who stows himself away can stow valuables too, so the hiding verb gains a with-phrase for the loot.
senses.whyCN: 藏匿者也可藏匿财物，藏身动词因此带上 with 短语表示赃物。

senses.title: To slip away quietly to avoid duty
senses.definition: to leave a place or duty without notice, avoiding responsibility
senses.definitionCN: 不打招呼便离开岗位或职责所在之地
senses.example: The guard absconded from his post at the border.
senses.exampleCN: 哨兵擅离了边境哨位。
senses.why: Hiding need not involve crime; avoiding an assigned watch keeps only the vanishing image.
senses.whyCN: 藏匿未必涉罪；逃避值勤只保留「消失不见」这一意象。

intro.en: Abscond comes from Latin abscondere 'to hide away', from abs- (variant of ab-) 'away' and condere 'to put together, store'.
intro.cn: abscond 来自拉丁语 abscondere「藏起来」，由 abs-（ab- 的变体）「离去」加 condere「收存、放置」构成。

items.en: Condere meant to put or store something safely, the root behind condiment and county through condo 'I found or store'.
items.cn: condere 义为妥善收存，是 condiment 等词的词根，源自 condo「建立、贮存」。

items.en: Abscondere added the away-prefix: to stow something or oneself out of sight.
items.cn: abscondere 加上离去前缀：把某物或自己藏到视线之外。

items.en: Absconditus, the participle, described anything kept hidden.
items.cn: 分词 absconditus 描述一切被藏匿之物。

items.en: The verb entered legal English describing fugitives and debtors in hiding.
items.cn: 十六世纪该动词进入法律英语，描述藏匿的逃犯与债务人。

items.en: The with-phrase spread as colonial reports recorded clerks absconding with funds.
items.cn: 十七至十八世纪，殖民记录频繁出现职员携款潜逃，with 短语随之流行。

items.en: It remains formal and legal, used of bail jumping, theft flights, and desertions.
items.cn: 如今仍属正式法律用语，用于弃保潜逃、盗窃外逃与擅离职守。

note.en: The first group is the condere hiding family; the second lists flight verbs.
note.cn: 第一组为 condere 藏匿词族；第二组为表逃走的动词。

entries.definition: the common past participle used in warrants and reports.
entries.definitionCN: 常用过去分词，见于通缉令与报告。

entries.definition: hidden away from company; from se- plus cludere, a different but parallel hiding verb.
entries.definitionCN: 隐居避世的；由 se- 加 cludere 构成，是平行的另一藏匿动词。

entries.definition: done secretly; shares the idea of stealth but uses the rapere root.
entries.definitionCN: 偷偷进行的；同样表隐秘，但用的是 rapere 词根。

entries.definition: to desert entirely; looks close but has a different root.
entries.definitionCN: 完全遗弃；拼写相近但词根不同。

entries.definition: rare nominal form for the act of absconding.
entries.definitionCN: 潜逃行为的罕见名词形式。

entries.definition: to run away quickly, without the necessary secrecy.
entries.definitionCN: 迅速逃离，不必隐秘。

entries.definition: to depart suddenly and secretly, originally of an army striking camp.
entries.definitionCN: 突然秘密离开，原指军队拔营。

entries.definition: to leave town hurriedly, especially to dodge debts.
entries.definitionCN: 匆匆离城，尤指躲债，口语说法。

entries.definition: to escape pursuit by cunning; the hiding is active toward pursuers.
entries.definitionCN: 以机智摆脱追捕；主动躲避追者。

entries.definition: to come back; the opposite of absconding from a place.
entries.definitionCN: 返回；与潜逃离开相反。

normalIntro.en: Take the word apart as abs- plus the storing root.
normalIntro.cn: 把单词拆成 abs- 加「收存」词根来记。

normal.en: abs- away + condere store = stow yourself away.
normal.cn: abs- 离去 + condere 收存 = 把自己藏起来。

normal.en: condere also lives in condiment, something stored up.
normal.cn: condere 还活在 condiment 里，即「收存之物」。

normal.en: Fixed pattern: abscond with + loot, abscond from + place.
normal.cn: 固定搭配：abscond with + 赃物，abscond from + 地点。

normal.en: Legal reports love the participle absconded.
normal.cn: 法律文书偏爱分词形式 absconded。

normal.en: Contrast flee: abscond always adds secrecy.
normal.cn: 与 flee 对照：abscond 必含隐秘。

abstract.en: Picture a figure slipping out the back gate at midnight.
abstract.cn: 想象一个身影午夜从后门溜走。

abstract.en: Hear no door sound at all: the vanishing is silent.
abstract.cn: 门声全无：消失是无声的。

abstract.en: See a bag of cash swinging as its owner runs.
abstract.cn: 看一袋现金随主人奔逃而晃动。

examples.en: The accountant absconded with nearly a million dollars.
examples.cn: 会计卷走近百万美元潜逃。

examples.en: The prisoner absconded during a work detail outside the fence.
examples.cn: 囚犯在围栏外劳动时趁机潜逃。

examples.en: Rather than face the creditors, he absconded from the city.
examples.cn: 他不去面对债主，而是从城中悄然遁走。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「我不扛的」——钱我不扛了，人先溜了。

root: 拉丁语 abscondere：abs-（ab- 变体，离去）+ condere（收存、放置，词根 cond-/cond- 见于 condiment）。本义「藏而不见」，经法律英语专化为「潜逃、藏匿避捕」，十八世纪起又固定出「携物而逃」的 with 搭配。

sensesIntro.en: One image of vanishing into hiding branches into fugitive flight, theft, and desertion.
sensesIntro.cn: 「隐入藏匿」一个意象分出逃匿、携赃与擅离三枝。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a figure stowing itself away out of sight.
core.cn: 核心意象：身影把自己藏到视线之外。

branches.en: FUGITIVE: debtors and prisoners disappear until pursuit fades.
branches.cn: 逃匿者：债务人、囚犯消失至追捕止息。

branches.en: EMBEZZLEMENT: the with-phrase ties flight to stolen funds.
branches.cn: 侵占：with 短语把潜逃与赃款绑在一起。

branches.en: DESERTION: posts and duties left without notice.
branches.cn: 擅离：哨位与职责无人而别。

branches.en: SECRECY CORE: every sense keeps the unseen departure.
branches.cn: 隐秘内核：各义项都保留「无声离去」。

branches.en: LEGAL REGISTER: warrants name the absconded clerk.
branches.cn: 法律语域：通缉令直书 absconded。

intro.en: The condere storing root builds a quiet family of hidden things.
intro.cn: condere 收存词根构建了一个关于藏匿的安静词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin verbs of storing and hiding persist in formal English.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语的贮存与藏匿动词留存于正式英语。

definition_zh: 缺席；不在；缺乏；没有
definition_en: the state of not being present, or the lack of something
core_image: 教室里一把空着的椅子
scene: 点名时，老师发现最后一排少了一个人。The teacher noticed his absence at roll call.
sceneCN: 这里的 absence 指「缺席」（第 1 个义项：人不在场）；句意是点名时老师发现他缺席。

derivatives.zh: 义为「缺席的；不在的」
义为「心不在焉地」

senses.title: Not being present
senses.definition: the state of a person not being in a place
senses.definitionCN: 某人不在某处的状态
senses.example: The teacher noticed his absence at roll call.
senses.exampleCN: 点名时老师发现他缺席。
senses.why: The Latin noun names being away, and a missing person is the plainest case.
senses.whyCN: 这个拉丁名词指「不在」，缺席的人是最直白的例子。

senses.title: Lack of something
senses.definition: the state of not having something needed
senses.definitionCN: 缺少某样必需之物的状态
senses.example: The absence of clean water slowed the work.
senses.exampleCN: 缺乏干净的水拖慢了工作。
senses.why: If a thing is not there, it is absent, and the noun covers it as well as people.
senses.whyCN: 某物不在就是缺失，名词既指人也指物。

senses.title: A period away
senses.definition: a length of time spent away from a place
senses.definitionCN: 不在某地的一段时期
senses.example: After a long absence he returned to the town.
senses.exampleCN: 离开很久之后，他回到了镇上。
senses.why: Away is also a duration, so the noun measures the time of not being there.
senses.whyCN: 「不在」也有一段时长，名词便计量这段不在的时间。

senses.title: Absence of mind
senses.definition: in absence of mind, a lack of attention to what is happening
senses.definitionCN: 在 absence of mind 中，指对眼前之事缺乏注意
senses.example: He signed the wrong line in a moment of absence.
senses.exampleCN: 他一时分神，签错了行。
senses.why: The mind can be away while the body stays, and the word follows it.
senses.whyCN: 身体在而心可以不在，这个词便跟着心走。

senses.title: Official leave
senses.definition: in leave of absence, permission to be away from duty
senses.definitionCN: 在 leave of absence 中，指获准离开岗位
senses.example: She took a year's leave of absence to travel.
senses.exampleCN: 她请了一年假去旅行。
senses.why: An approved absence is still an absence, only a permitted one.
senses.whyCN: 获准的缺席仍是缺席，只是被允许了。

senses.title: A missing proof
senses.definition: in absence of evidence, the lack of proof for a claim
senses.definitionCN: 在 absence of evidence 中，指主张缺少证据
senses.example: The case failed for absence of evidence.
senses.exampleCN: 此案因证据缺失而未能成立。
senses.why: Law reasons from what is not there, and the word names that gap.
senses.whyCN: 法律会从「不存在的东西」推理，这个词便指那道缺口。

senses.title: Emotional distance
senses.definition: a felt lack of warmth or presence in a relationship
senses.definitionCN: 关系中缺少温暖或陪伴的感觉
senses.example: The child felt her father's absence even at home.
senses.exampleCN: 即使在家，孩子也能感到父亲的疏离。
senses.why: A person can be physically near and still absent in feeling.
senses.whyCN: 人可以身在近处，情感上却仍然缺席。

senses.title: Acting in someone's place
senses.definition: in in someone's absence, the time when another acts for them
senses.definitionCN: 在 in someone's absence 中，指由他人代为行事之时
senses.example: In the manager's absence, she signed the order.
senses.exampleCN: 经理不在时，她签了这份订单。
senses.why: The gap left by one person becomes the space where another acts.
senses.whyCN: 一个人留下的空位，成了另一个人行事的空间。

definition_en: a formal release from guilt, sin, or obligation
core_image: 一笔勾销，枷锁落地

senses.title: Formal forgiveness of sins
senses.definition: the formal declaration by a priest or church that sin is forgiven
senses.definitionCN: 由神父或教会正式宣告罪得赦免
senses.example: After confession the penitent knelt to receive absolution.
senses.exampleCN: 告解之后，忏悔者跪领赦罪。
senses.why: Latin solvere means to loosen; what sin bound, the declared pardon unties.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 solvere 义为解开；罪所缚者，经宣告的赦免解开。

senses.title: Release from blame or duty
senses.definition: the freeing of a person from responsibility, fault, or a promise
senses.definitionCN: 使某人免除责任、过错或诺言约束
senses.example: The inquiry gave the pilot full absolution for the crash.
senses.exampleCN: 调查认定飞行员对坠机不负任何责任。
senses.why: Loosening a bond works as well for legal duty as for sin, so the church word spread to law.
senses.whyCN: 「解开束缚」既适用于罪，也适用于法律责任，教会用语因此扩入法律。

senses.title: Remission of a penalty
senses.definition: the cancellation of an imposed punishment or obligation
senses.definitionCN: 取消已施加的惩罚或义务
senses.example: The king's letter won absolution of the fine.
senses.exampleCN: 国王的手谕使他免除了罚金。
senses.why: A penalty is a weight attached to the offender; cancelling it is one more kind of untying.
senses.whyCN: 刑罚是系于过错者身上的重负，取消它不过是又一次「解绳」。

intro.en: Absolution comes from Latin absolutio, the noun of absolvere 'to loosen from', from ab- 'from' and solvere 'to loosen'.
intro.cn: absolution 来自拉丁语 absolutio，是 absolvere「解脱」的名词，由 ab-「从……离去」加 solvere「解开」构成。

items.en: A root *leu- meant to loosen, split, or untie, the distant source of solvere and of lite words.
items.cn: 词根 *leu- 义为松开、解开，是 solvere 与 lite 类词的远源。

items.en: Solvere meant to untie, pay off, or release, used of debts and chains alike.
items.cn: solvere 义为解开、偿清、释放，既用于债务也用于锁链。

items.en: Absolvere added ab- 'from': to loose someone from a bond, hence to acquit.
items.cn: absolvere 加上 ab-「从」：把人从束缚中松开，引申为开释。

items.en: Absolutio became the technical term for the priestly declaration of pardon.
items.cn: absolutio 成为神父宣告赦罪的术语。

items.en: Absolucion passed into French with both religious and legal uses.
items.cn: absolucion 进入法语，兼有宗教与法律两用。

items.en: The word settled in English liturgy and law, keeping both branches alive.
items.cn: 该词在英语礼仪与法律语域定型，两支语义并行至今。

senses.title: To declare sins forgiven
senses.definition: of a priest or church, to declare formally that a person's sins are forgiven
senses.definitionCN: 神父或教会正式宣告某人之罪已获赦免
senses.example: The priest absolved the dying sailor and closed the book.
senses.exampleCN: 神父赦免了垂死水手的罪，合上了经书。
senses.why: Sin is a knot that binds the soul; the priest's word unties it.
senses.whyCN: 罪是缚住灵魂的绳结，神父的话语将其解开。

senses.title: To free from blame or responsibility
senses.definition: to declare a person free of fault, guilt, or a duty in a legal or moral sense
senses.definitionCN: 在法律或道德层面宣告某人无过错、无责任
senses.example: The audit absolved the treasurer of mishandling funds.
senses.exampleCN: 审计表明司库并无挪用资金之责。
senses.why: A duty binds like a chain; the same loosening image frees people from blame.
senses.whyCN: 责任如锁链缚身，同一「解绳」意象把人从责难中释放。

senses.title: To release from a promise or obligation
senses.definition: to free somebody from the binding force of a vow, promise, or contract duty
senses.definitionCN: 使人摆脱誓言、诺言或合同义务的约束
senses.example: The bankruptcy court absolved him from the old debts.
senses.exampleCN: 破产法庭免除了他的旧债。
senses.why: An obligation is a tie; absolving is cutting the tie, whatever it holds.
senses.whyCN: 义务是绳索，赦免即断绳，无论绳所系者为何。

intro.en: Absolve comes from Latin absolvere 'to loosen from, acquit', from ab- 'from' and solvere 'to loosen, pay'.
intro.cn: absolve 来自拉丁语 absolvere「解脱、开释」，由 ab-「从」加 solvere「解开、偿付」构成。

items.en: The reconstructed root *leu- meant to loosen or untie, generally regarded as the origin of solvere.
items.cn: 重构词根 *leu- 义为松开、解开，一般认为是 solvere 的来源。

items.en: Solvere covered untying, paying off, and releasing, from knots to debts.
items.cn: solvere 涵盖解开、偿清与释放，从绳结到债务皆可。

items.en: Absolvere, with ab-, became the verb of acquitting a defendant.
items.cn: absolvere 带前缀 ab-，成为开释被告的动词。

items.en: The verb named the priest's act of forgiving sin in confession.
items.cn: 该动词在教会拉丁语中指神父于告解中赦罪。

items.en: Absouldre entered French and then English in both religious and legal texts.
items.cn: absouldre 先入法语，再随宗教与法律文本进入英语。

items.en: English usage settled with two prepositions, of and from, marking guilt and duty respectively.
items.cn: 英语用法定型于 of 与 from 两个介词，分别引出罪责与义务。

sensesIntro.en: Loosening a bond spreads from forgiving sin to clearing blame and cutting obligations.

branches.en: CHURCH: the priest's word unties sin.

branches.en: COURT AND ENQUIRY: evidence unties blame.

branches.en: OF OR FROM: the preposition names what was tied.

scene: 孩子把故事书抱在怀里，读得忘了吃饭。She was so absorbed in the story that she forgot dinner.

senses.title: To hold attention completely
senses.definition: takes up all of someone's attention
senses.definitionCN: 占据某人的全部注意力
senses.example: She was so absorbed in the story that she forgot dinner.
senses.exampleCN: 她读得太入迷，忘了晚饭。
senses.why: Attention is drawn in the way a sponge draws water, which is the root image.
senses.whyCN: 注意力被吸进去，正如海绵吸水，这是词根的意象。

senses.title: To take in liquid
senses.definition: soaks up a liquid into itself
senses.definitionCN: 把液体吸进自身
senses.example: The cloth absorbed the spilled milk.
senses.exampleCN: 布吸干了洒出的牛奶。
senses.why: The Latin verb means to suck in, and liquid is its first object.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁动词意为「吸进」，液体是它最早的对象。

senses.title: To take in energy
senses.definition: takes in light, heat or sound rather than reflecting it
senses.definitionCN: 吸收光、热或声，而不是把它们反射出去
senses.example: Dark surfaces absorb more heat than light ones.
senses.exampleCN: 深色表面比浅色表面吸收更多热量。
senses.why: The same sucking-in model applies to invisible things such as heat.
senses.whyCN: 同样的「吸进」模型适用于热这类看不见的东西。

senses.title: To understand and retain
senses.definition: takes in information and makes it one's own
senses.definitionCN: 接收信息并把它变成自己的
senses.example: Students need time to absorb the new material.
senses.exampleCN: 学生需要时间消化新材料。
senses.why: Knowledge is treated as something poured in and held, like liquid in cloth.
senses.whyCN: 知识被当作可以倒入并留住的东西，如同布中的水。

senses.title: To take over a group
senses.definition: makes a smaller organisation part of a larger one
senses.definitionCN: 使较小的组织并入较大的组织
senses.example: The bank absorbed two small rivals.
senses.exampleCN: 这家银行吞并了两个小竞争对手。
senses.why: One body takes another into itself, and the word comes from physical soaking.
senses.whyCN: 一个实体把另一个纳入自身，这个词源自物理上的吸入。

senses.title: To use up time or money
senses.definition: takes up a share of time, money or effort
senses.definitionCN: 占去一部分时间、金钱或精力
senses.example: The repairs absorbed most of the budget.
senses.exampleCN: 维修耗去了大部分预算。
senses.why: A cost taken in leaves less of the whole, like liquid taken up by cloth.
senses.whyCN: 被吸走的成本使总量减少，如同布吸走液体。

senses.title: To soften an impact
senses.definition: takes the force of a blow and reduces it
senses.definitionCN: 承受冲击并使其减弱
senses.example: The thick mat absorbed the fall.
senses.exampleCN: 厚垫子缓冲了坠落。
senses.why: A blow taken into a material is no longer felt as a blow.
senses.whyCN: 冲击被材料吸收，就不再作为冲击被感觉到。

senses.title: To take in nutrients
senses.definition: in biology, takes nutrients through a surface
senses.definitionCN: 生物学上指通过表面吸收养分
senses.example: Roots absorb water and minerals from the soil.
senses.exampleCN: 根从土壤中吸收水分和矿物质。
senses.why: Living tissue taking in what it needs is the biological face of soaking up.
senses.whyCN: 活组织摄入所需之物，正是「吸入」的生物学面貌。

definition_en: the taking in of a liquid, gas, nutrient, energy, or knowledge, and the state of being completely engaged or merged into something larger
core_image: 一块干海绵贴到水面上，水沿着孔隙往上走，表面很快变暗变重。
scene: 雨刚停，田里那块黏土地还按着水不放，农机一开进去就打了滑。The absorption of water by the clay soil delayed the planting.
