senses.title: The uptake of liquid by a material
senses.definition: the process by which a solid takes a liquid into itself, filling its pores or spaces
senses.definitionCN: 固体把液体纳入自身、填满孔隙或空隙的过程
senses.example: The absorption of water by the clay soil delayed the planting.
senses.exampleCN: 黏土对水的吸收延误了播种。
senses.why: Latin absorbere is to suck in. The image is not a surface coating but a material pulling something inside itself.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 absorbere 是“吸进去”。画面不是表面涂层，而是材料把某物拉进自身内部。

senses.title: The body's uptake of nutrients
senses.titleCN: 吸收营养：穿过肠壁进了身体
senses.definition: the passage of digested nutrients into the blood or body tissues
senses.definitionCN: 消化后的营养进入血液或身体组织的过程
senses.example: Poor absorption of iron can cause fatigue.
senses.exampleCN: 铁吸收不良会导致疲劳。
senses.why: The body is the container here. Nutrients are not merely eaten but taken through a wall into the interior.
senses.whyCN: 这里的容器是身体。营养不只是被吃下，而是穿过一道壁进入内部。

senses.title: The taking in of knowledge
senses.titleCN: 知识的吸收：读进去、化成自己的
senses.definition: the process of understanding and remembering information so that it becomes part of one's knowledge
senses.definitionCN: 理解并记住信息，使其成为自身知识一部分的过程
senses.example: The course depends on steady absorption of new vocabulary.
senses.exampleCN: 这门课依赖对新词汇的稳定吸收。
senses.why: Learning is treated as a material process: what is read is absorbed into the mind as water is absorbed into a cloth.
senses.whyCN: 学习被当作材料过程：读到的东西被吸进心里，就像水被吸进布中。

senses.title: Complete engrossment in an activity
senses.titleCN: 专注：整个人被吸进一件事
senses.definition: the state of having all one's attention taken by something, so that time and surroundings drop away
senses.definitionCN: 全部注意力被某事物占据，时间与周围环境都退去的状态
senses.example: His absorption in the problem made him miss the last train.
senses.exampleCN: 他对那个问题的专注让他错过了末班车。
senses.why: The same verb that takes liquid into a sponge takes a person into a task. The mind has no attention left on the surface.
senses.whyCN: 把水吸进海绵的那个动词，也把人吸进一项任务。心智在表面上再没留下注意力。

senses.title: The merging of an organisation
senses.titleCN: 并入：小公司被大公司吞进去
senses.definition: the incorporation of one company, group, or territory into a larger one, losing separate identity
senses.definitionCN: 一个公司、团体或地区被并入更大者，失去独立身份
senses.example: The absorption of the smaller firm took two years to complete.
senses.exampleCN: 对那家较小公司的并入花了两年才完成。
senses.why: Corporate absorption keeps the physical picture: the smaller body is taken inside the larger and no longer has an outer surface of its own.
senses.whyCN: 公司“并入”保留了物理画面：较小的实体被纳入更大者内部，不再有自己的外表面。

senses.title: The uptake of light or energy
senses.definition: the process in which matter takes up electromagnetic radiation or energy, often converting it into heat
senses.definitionCN: 物质摄取电磁辐射或能量、常将其转为热的过程
senses.example: The dark surface showed strong absorption across the visible spectrum.
senses.exampleCN: 深色表面在整个可见光谱上表现出强吸收。
senses.why: Physics names with the old verb: a photon is not reflected or transmitted but swallowed by the material.
senses.whyCN: 物理学沿用这个古老动词：光子不被反射或透射，而是被材料吞掉。

senses.title: The dissolving of a gas in a liquid
senses.titleCN: 溶解吸收：气体进了液体里面
senses.definition: the process by which gas molecules enter the bulk of a liquid rather than staying on its surface
senses.definitionCN: 气体分子进入液体内部、而非停留在表面的过程
senses.example: The absorption of carbon dioxide by seawater lowers the ocean's pH.
senses.exampleCN: 海水对二氧化碳的吸收降低了海洋的 pH。
senses.why: Chemistry distinguishes absorption from adsorption: here the gas goes inside the liquid, not onto a surface.
senses.whyCN: 化学区分 absorption 与 adsorption：这里气体进入液体内部，而不是附着在表面。

senses.title: The damping of sound
senses.definition: the reduction of sound energy as it passes into a material, so that less is reflected back
senses.definitionCN: 声音进入材料时能量被削减、反射回来的部分减少
senses.example: The studio's walls were chosen for their low-frequency absorption.
senses.exampleCN: 录音室的墙是按低频吸声性能挑选的。
senses.why: Sound is a wave, and a porous wall takes part of it in. The energy does not vanish; it becomes a little heat inside the material.
senses.whyCN: 声音是波，多孔的墙把其中一部分收进去。能量并未消失，而是在材料内部变成一点热。

intro.en: Absorption is Latin absorptio, from absorbere 'to suck in': ab- 'away' plus sorbere 'to suck'. English borrowed the noun in the 16c and later gave it technical work in physics and chemistry.
intro.cn: absorption 是拉丁语 absorptio，来自 absorbere“吸进去”：ab-“离开”加 sorbere“吸”。英语 16 世纪借入这个名词，后来才在物理与化学中给它技术任务。

items.en: To suck in, swallow, or drink up. It describes a mouth or a porous body drawing something inward.
items.cn: 吸入、吞下、喝干。它描述嘴或多孔的身体把某物向内拉。

items.en: Away from, off. With sorbere it marks the movement of something out of its surroundings and into the absorbing body.
items.cn: 离开、脱离。与 sorbere 结合，标记某物从周围环境进入吸收者内部。

items.en: To swallow up, to take in completely. It is used of the sea swallowing a ship as well as of a sponge taking water.
items.cn: 吞没、完全纳入。它既用于大海吞没船只，也用于海绵吸水。

items.en: A swallowing up. The noun is rare in classical Latin but exactly matches the English technical need.
items.cn: 吞没、吸尽。这个名词在古典拉丁语中不常见，却正好对应英语的技术需要。

items.en: The noun enters English through learned writing. Early uses are medical and alchemical before they become physical.
items.cn: 这个名词经学术写作进入英语。早期用法属医学与炼金术，之后才转为物理学用法。

items.en: Physics, chemistry, acoustics, and business each take a share: light, gas, sound, nutrients, and companies are all absorbed. The mental sense, absorbed in a book, keeps the oldest metaphor alive.
items.cn: 物理学、化学、声学与商业各取一份：光、气体、声音、营养、公司都能被“吸收”。心智义“沉浸在一本书里”让最古老的比喻继续活着。

note.en: The first group is the absorb family plus adsorption, a look-alike with a different prefix and a genuinely different process; the second compares other kinds of taking in.
note.cn: 第一组是 absorb 词族，外加 adsorption——一个前缀不同、过程也确实不同的形近词；第二组比较其他“纳入”方式。

entries.definition: to take in liquid, energy, or information. The verb is the act; absorption is the process or state.
entries.definitionCN: 吸收液体、能量或信息；动词指动作，absorption 指过程或状态。

entries.definition: able to absorb, or a material that does so. It describes capacity, not an event.
entries.definitionCN: 能吸收的，或指吸收材料；描述能力，而非事件。

entries.definition: relating to absorption. It often appears in technical phrases such as absorptive capacity.
entries.definitionCN: 与吸收有关的，常见于 absorptive capacity 等技术短语。

entries.definition: the sticking of molecules onto a surface. It uses ad- 'to' rather than ab- 'away', and is a surface process, not an uptake into the bulk.
entries.definitionCN: 分子附着在表面。它用 ad-“向”而非 ab-“离开”，是表面过程，不是吸入内部。

entries.definition: the taking in of a substance by a cell, tissue, or system. It is the neutral scientific partner.
entries.definitionCN: 细胞、组织或系统对物质的摄取；是中性的科学伙伴。

entries.definition: the process of absorbing information or a group so that it becomes part of the whole. It stresses integration after uptake.
entries.definitionCN: 把信息或群体吸收进来、使之成为整体一部分；强调摄入之后的整合。

entries.definition: the formal merging of one body into another. It is the legal form of the corporate sense.
entries.definitionCN: 一个实体正式并入另一个；是公司义的法律形式。

entries.definition: the state of having one's attention completely occupied. It is the mental sense without the physical image.
entries.definitionCN: 注意力被完全占据的状态；是去掉物理意象的心智义。

entries.definition: the reduction in strength of a signal or wave. It names the result of acoustic absorption, not the taking in.
entries.definitionCN: 信号或波强度的减弱；命名吸声的结果，而非“吸进去”的动作。

normalIntro.en: Real parts only: ab- 'away' plus sorbere 'to suck'. The same root gives absorb, absorbent, and absorptive; adsorption is a different prefix and a different process.
normalIntro.cn: 只用真实成分：ab-“离开”加 sorbere“吸”。同一词根给出 absorb、absorbent、absorptive；adsorption 前缀不同，过程也不同。

normal.en: Ab- away, sorb suck: absorption is something sucked away into another body.
normal.cn: ab- 离开，sorb 吸：absorption 就是某物被吸走、进入另一个物体。

normal.en: A sponge does not coat itself with water; it pulls the water inside.
normal.cn: 海绵不是给自己涂上一层水，而是把水拉进内部。

normal.en: Adsorption sticks to the surface; absorption goes into the bulk. One letter, two processes.
normal.cn: adsorption 贴在表面，absorption 进入内部。差一个字母，是两种过程。

normal.en: Absorbed in a book: the reader has been taken inside the text.
normal.cn: absorbed in a book：读者被吸进文本里面。

normal.en: A dark wall absorbs light and turns it into a little heat.
normal.cn: 深色的墙吸收光，并把它变成一点热。

abstract.en: Absorption is what happens when a boundary lets something through instead of bouncing it back.
abstract.cn: 吸收，就是边界让某物通过、而不是把它弹回去。

abstract.en: To be absorbed is to have no surface left for the world.
abstract.cn: 被吸进去，就是再没有留给世界的表面。

abstract.en: Matter, mind, and companies all have pores.
abstract.cn: 物质、心智与公司，都有孔隙。

examples.en: The root hairs increase the absorption of water from the soil.
examples.cn: 根毛增加了对土壤中水的吸收。

examples.en: His absorption in the chess game made the room seem to disappear.
examples.cn: 他对棋局的专注让整个房间仿佛消失了。

examples.en: The fabric's sound absorption was measured in a test chamber.
examples.cn: 这种织物的吸声性能在测试舱中被测量。

dict_mnemonic.text: “额不吸哦普申”——海绵“额”一下把水吸进去 → absorption 吸收

root: 源自拉丁语 absorptio，来自 absorbere（ab-“离开”+ sorbere“吸、吞”），本义“吸进去、吞没”；核心是“把外部之物纳入内部”。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses of absorption, one movement: something outside passes a boundary and becomes part of what is inside. The boundary can be a pore, a gut wall, a mind, a company, or a surface.
sensesIntro.cn: absorption 的八个义项只有一个动作：外部之物越过一道边界，成为内部的一部分。边界可以是孔隙、肠壁、心智、公司，或一个表面。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a dry sponge touching water and pulling it up into its pores.
core.cn: 核心意象：一块干海绵触到水面，把水往上拉进孔里。

branches.en: MATERIAL UPTAKE: a sponge and a seawater sample both pull a substance inside, one through pores and one through a liquid surface.
branches.cn: 材料摄入：海绵与海水样本都把物质拉进内部，一个经孔隙，一个经液面。

branches.en: THE BODY: nutrients cross a wall and become part of the organism.
branches.cn: 身体：营养穿过一道壁，成为生物体的一部分。

branches.en: THE MIND: knowledge is taken in, and a task can take the whole person in.
branches.cn: 心智：知识被吸进去，一项任务也能把整个人吸进去。

branches.en: THE ORGANISATION: a smaller firm loses its outer surface inside a larger one.
branches.cn: 组织：较小的公司在更大者内部失去自己的外表面。

branches.en: ENERGY AND SOUND: light and sound are swallowed and turned into heat rather than sent back.
branches.cn: 能量与声音：光与声被吞下、转为热，而不是被送回。

intro.en: Absorption carries Latin ab- and -tion. English builds the verb absorb, the capacity adjective absorbent, and the relational adjective absorptive.
intro.cn: absorption 带着拉丁前缀 ab- 与后缀 -tion。英语造出动词 absorb、能力形容词 absorbent，以及关系形容词 absorptive。

latinIntro.en: The Latin chain is sorbere 'to suck', absorbere 'to suck in', and absorptio 'a swallowing up'. Adsorption is not in this chain: it uses ad- and means surface attachment.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语链条是 sorbere“吸”、absorbere“吸进去”、absorptio“吞没”。adsorption 不在这个链条里：它用 ad-，意为表面附着。

items.meaning: to take in liquid, energy, or information
items.meaningCN: 吸收液体、能量或信息（拉丁动词英语化）
items.example: The paper towel absorbed the spill.
items.exampleCN: 纸巾吸干了洒出来的液体。

items.meaning: able to absorb; a material that absorbs
items.meaningCN: 能吸收的；吸收材料（-ent 构成形容词或名词）
与吸收有关的（-ive 构成关系形容词）
items.example: The absorptive capacity of the soil is low.
items.exampleCN: 这种土壤的吸收能力很低。

items.meaning: the process or state of being absorbed
items.meaningCN: 吸收的过程或被吸收的状态（-ion 构成动作名词）
items.example: Absorption of the drug is fastest on an empty stomach.

items.meaningCN: 自我专注；只顾自己（复合名词）
items.exampleCN: 他的自我专注让团队合作变得困难。

items.meaning: the pattern of wavelengths a substance takes in
items.meaningCN: 物质所吸收波长的图谱（技术复合词）
items.example: The absorption spectrum identified the gas.
items.exampleCN: 吸收光谱确定了这种气体。

items.meaning: the speed at which a substance is taken in
items.meaningCN: 物质被吸收的速度（技术复合词）
items.example: The absorption rate depends on temperature.

items.meaning: the uptake of water by a material or body
items.meaningCN: 材料或身体对水的吸收（固定短语）
items.example: The absorption of water by the seeds begins within minutes.
items.exampleCN: 种子对水的吸收在几分钟内就开始。

items.meaning: the damping of sound energy by a material
items.meaningCN: 材料对声能的削减（复合词）
items.example: The ceiling panels improve sound absorption.
items.exampleCN: 天花板板材改善了吸声效果。

items.meaning: the merging of a firm into another
items.meaningCN: 一家公司被并入另一家（商业短语）
items.example: The absorption of the company removed its brand from the market.
items.exampleCN: 该公司的并入使其品牌从市场上消失。

definition_zh: 抽象的；抽象作品；摘要；提取
definition_en: existing as an idea rather than a physical thing, or a short summary
core_image: 一幅只画了几何色块的画
scene: 美术馆里，一幅没有具体形象的画让人停下来看。The gallery showed an abstract painting with no clear subject.
sceneCN: 这里的 abstract 指「抽象的」（第 1 个义项：不以具体形象呈现）；句意是美术馆展出一幅没有明确主题的抽象画。

derivatives.zh: 加 -ion 构成，义为「抽象；抽象概念」
义为「抽象地」
义为「出神的；心不在焉的」

senses.title: Not concrete
senses.definition: existing as an idea, not as a physical object
senses.definitionCN: 作为观念而存在，而非具体物体
senses.example: The gallery showed an abstract painting with no clear subject.
senses.exampleCN: 美术馆展出一幅没有明确主题的抽象画。
senses.why: The Latin participle means drawn away, and an idea drawn away from things is abstract.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁分词意为「被抽走」，从具体事物中抽出的观念就是抽象的。

senses.title: Abstract art
senses.definition: art that does not try to show real objects
senses.definitionCN: 不试图表现真实物体的艺术
senses.example: She prefers abstract to landscape painting.
senses.exampleCN: 比起风景画，她更喜欢抽象画。
senses.why: Art that draws away from likeness keeps the word for what has been removed.
senses.whyCN: 从形似中抽离的艺术，保留了这个「被抽走」的词。

senses.title: A summary
senses.definition: a short account of the main points of a paper
senses.definitionCN: 对论文要点的简短陈述
senses.example: Read the abstract before the full paper.
senses.exampleCN: 先读摘要，再读全文。
senses.why: A summary draws the essence out of a longer text.
senses.whyCN: 摘要就是把要点从长文中抽出来。

senses.title: To extract
senses.definition: takes something out of a larger mass
senses.definitionCN: 从较大的整体中取出某物
senses.example: The process abstracts metal from ore.
senses.exampleCN: 这道工序从矿石中提取金属。
senses.why: The literal sense of drawing away survives in chemistry and mining.
senses.whyCN: 「抽走」的字面义在化学与采矿中留存。

senses.title: In the abstract
senses.definition: in the phrase in the abstract, considered apart from real cases
senses.definitionCN: 在 in the abstract 中，指脱离具体事例来考虑
senses.example: In the abstract, the plan sounds fair.
senses.exampleCN: 从理论上说，这个计划听起来很公平。
senses.why: To consider apart from cases is to draw the idea away from them.
senses.whyCN: 脱离事例来考虑，就是把观念从事例中抽走。

senses.title: An abstract noun
senses.definition: a noun naming a quality or state rather than a thing
senses.definitionCN: 指称性质或状态而非物体的名词
senses.example: Freedom is an abstract noun.
senses.exampleCN: 自由是一个抽象名词。
senses.why: Grammar classifies words by whether they name something drawn away from matter.
senses.whyCN: 语法按是否指称脱离物质之物来分类名词。

senses.title: Lost in thought
senses.definition: in abstracted, with the mind drawn away from the present
senses.definitionCN: 在 abstracted 中，指心思离开了眼前
senses.example: He gave an abstracted reply and walked on.
senses.exampleCN: 他心不在焉地答了一句，继续往前走。
senses.why: A mind drawn away from the room is literally abstracted.
senses.whyCN: 心思被抽离房间，字面上就是被抽走。

senses.title: To remove in chemistry
senses.definition: in chemistry, separates a substance from a mixture
senses.definitionCN: 化学上从混合物中分离出某种物质
senses.example: The lab abstracts the active compound from the leaf.
senses.exampleCN: 实验室从叶子中萃取活性成分。
senses.why: Chemical extraction is the modern technical heir of drawing something out.
senses.whyCN: 化学萃取正是「把某物抽出」的现代技术后裔。

intro.en: The word comes from a Latin verb meaning to draw away.
intro.cn: 这个词出自意为「抽走」的拉丁语动词。

items.en: trahere meant to draw or pull.
items.cn: trahere 意为拉、牵引。

items.en: abstrahere added ab-, away, to mean draw off.
items.cn: abstrahere 加 ab-（离开），意为抽走。

items.en: abstractus meant drawn away or removed.
items.cn: abstractus 意为被抽走的、被移开的。

items.en: abstract entered English as a term of logic.
items.cn: abstract 作为逻辑术语进入英语。

items.en: the noun sense of a summary appeared.
items.cn: 名词「摘要」义出现。

items.en: the word spread to art, chemistry and grammar.
items.cn: 这个词扩展到艺术、化学与语法。

note.en: The look-alike group is the abstract family; the near-meaning group is words of theory and summary.
note.cn: 形近组是 abstract 词族；近义组是表示理论与摘要的词。

entries.definition: in a theoretical way

entries.definition: with the mind elsewhere
entries.definitionCN: 出神的；心不在焉的

normalIntro.cn: 下面几条贴着拉丁语 abstrahere，意为「抽走」。

normal.en: trahere is to draw, and abs- draws away.
normal.cn: trahere 是拉，abs- 表示拉走。

abstract.en: See a shape with all details rubbed out.
abstract.cn: 想象一个细节被擦掉的形状。

abstract.cn: 想象速写被简化成几块颜色。

abstract.en: Think of a page boiled down to five lines.

sensesIntro.en: Drawing something away yields ideas, art, summaries, chemical extracts and a wandering mind.
sensesIntro.cn: 把东西抽走，生出观念、艺术、摘要、化学萃取与走神的心思。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a picture with all detail drawn away.
core.cn: 核心意象：细节被抽走的画面。

branches.en: ideas and abstract nouns
branches.cn: 观念与抽象名词

branches.en: art without likeness
branches.cn: 不追求形似的艺术

branches.en: a summary and theory apart from cases

branches.cn: 工业与化学中的提取

branches.cn: 被抽离的心思

intro.en: The word is a Latin participle with English uses as three parts of speech.
intro.cn: 这个词是拉丁分词，在英语中作三种词性使用。

latinIntro.en: The root trahere, to draw, also gives tractor and attract.
latinIntro.cn: 词根 trahere（拉）也生出 tractor 与 attract。

derivatives.zh: 义为「抽象」
义为「抽象地」

definition_zh: 荒谬的；荒唐的；可笑的；不合常理的
definition_en: so unreasonable or illogical that it seems laughable
core_image: 一个人一本正经地做一件根本讲不通的事
scene: 他举着伞站在雨里，却把伞面朝下扣在头顶。It seemed absurd to carry an umbrella upside down in a storm.
sceneCN: 这里 absurd 指行为荒唐可笑（第 1 个义项：荒谬可笑）；句意为在暴风雨里把伞倒着拿，实在荒唐。

derivatives.zh: 由形容词加 -ity 构成，义为「荒谬；荒唐事」
由形容词加 -ly 构成，义为「荒唐地；离谱地」
由形容词加 -ness 构成，义为「荒谬性」
由形容词加 -ism 构成，义为「荒诞主义」
由 absurdism 派生，义为「荒诞派作家或作品」

senses.title: So unreasonable as to be laughable
senses.definition: so clearly against reason that it makes people laugh or shake their heads
senses.definitionCN: 明显违背理性，让人发笑或摇头
senses.example: The plan was absurd from the start.
senses.exampleCN: 这个计划从一开始就荒谬。
senses.why: Latin absurdus described something out of tune, and a claim out of tune with reason sounds wrong to the ear.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 absurdus 描写「走调」的东西，与理性走调的说法听起来就不对。

senses.title: Contrary to common sense
senses.definition: opposed to what ordinary experience says must be true
senses.definitionCN: 与日常经验认定的必然情况相反
senses.example: It is absurd to expect a reply in an hour.
senses.exampleCN: 指望一小时内有回复是违背常理的。
senses.why: Common sense is the tuning fork, and whatever cannot match its note is absurd.
senses.whyCN: 常识是那把音叉，对不上它音高的东西就是荒谬的。

senses.title: Theatre of the Absurd
senses.definition: a style of drama showing human life as meaningless and comic
senses.definitionCN: 把人生表现为无意义又滑稽的戏剧风格
senses.example: Beckett's plays belong to the Theatre of the Absurd.
senses.exampleCN: 贝克特的戏剧属于荒诞派戏剧。
senses.why: The movement took the word's sense of broken logic and made it a whole stage world.
senses.whyCN: 这个流派借用了这个词「逻辑断裂」的含义，把它变成一个完整的舞台世界。

senses.title: Reductio ad absurdum
senses.definition: a proof that refutes a claim by showing its consequences to be absurd
senses.definitionCN: 通过展示某个主张的后果荒谬来驳倒它
senses.example: The argument ends in a reductio ad absurdum.
senses.exampleCN: 这个论证以归谬收场。
senses.why: Logic uses the word as a tool: push the opponent's rule until it produces its own absurd note.
senses.whyCN: 逻辑学把这个词当工具：把对方的规则推到它自己发出荒谬音高的地方。

intro.en: Absurd is Latin for out of tune, and its modern senses keep that musical idea of a note that does not fit.
intro.cn: absurd 在拉丁语中意为「走调」，它的现代义项都保留着「音符不合调」的音乐观念。

items.en: Modern English uses absurd for bad arguments, comic mismatches, and the human condition alike.
items.cn: 现代英语用 absurd 兼指糟糕的论证、滑稽的不相称与人的处境。

items.en: Twentieth-century drama gave the word a stage: plays in which logic itself breaks down.
items.cn: 二十世纪的戏剧给了这个词一个舞台：逻辑本身崩坏的戏。

items.en: Sixteenth-century English took the word from French absurde, mostly for statements that contradict reason.
items.cn: 十六世纪英语从法语 absurde 借入这个词，主要用于违背理性的陈述。

items.en: Latin absurdus meant out of tune or harsh-sounding, and by extension senseless.
items.cn: 拉丁语 absurdus 意为「走调的、刺耳的」，引申为「没有意义的」。

items.en: The second element is surdus, deaf or dull; scholars debate how exactly deafness produced the sense of discord.
items.cn: 第二个构件是 surdus「聋的、迟钝的」；学者对「聋」如何产生「不和谐」义仍有争论。

note.en: The look-alike group collects forms and nouns from the same out-of-tune root; the near-meaning group collects words for ridiculousness and illogic.
note.cn: 形近组收同一「走调」词根的形式与名词；近义组收表示可笑与不合逻辑的词。

entries.definition: The quality of being absurd, or an absurd thing.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「荒谬；荒唐事」。

entries.definition: In a way that is beyond reason.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「荒唐地；离谱地」。

entries.definition: The view that the universe lacks meaning.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「荒诞主义」。

entries.definition: A speech sound voiceless in articulation, or a root that cannot be expressed as a fraction.
entries.definitionCN: 名词或形容词，义为「清音；无理数」，与 absurd 同出 surdus。

entries.definition: Deserving or inviting laughter.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「可笑的；荒谬的」。

entries.definition: So foolish that it is laughable.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「荒唐可笑的」。

entries.definition: Not following the rules of reasoning.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「不合逻辑的」。

entries.definition: Completely contrary to reason or nature.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「荒谬的；反常理的」。

entries.definition: So inadequate that it causes laughter.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「可笑的；不值一提的」。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the musical idea of a note out of tune and the stages where the word became famous.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子用「音符走调」的音乐观念，以及这个词成名的舞台。

normal.en: Ab plus surd: surd means deaf or dull, so absurd is a note the ear refuses to accept.
normal.cn: ab 加 surd：surd 意为聋的、迟钝的，所以 absurd 是耳朵拒绝接受的音符。

normal.en: Imagine an orchestra where one cello plays a different song: that clash is absurd.
normal.cn: 想象一支乐队里有一把大提琴在拉另一首曲子：那种冲突就是荒谬。

normal.en: An absurd plan is a plan tuned to a different key from reality.
normal.cn: 荒唐的计划，就是调到与现实不同调的计划。

normal.en: The Theatre of the Absurd put the wrong note on stage for a whole evening.
normal.cn: 荒诞派戏剧把那个错音搬上舞台，演了一整晚。

normal.en: Reductio ad absurdum is logic's way of letting an argument play its own wrong note.
normal.cn: 归谬法是逻辑学让论证自己奏出那个错音的办法。

abstract.en: Picture two instruments playing the same tune in different keys: nothing is broken, yet nothing fits.
abstract.cn: 想象两件乐器用不同的调演奏同一支曲子：什么都没坏，却什么都合不上。

abstract.en: Every sense is that misfit: words, plans, pairs of objects, whole philosophies.
abstract.cn: 每个义项都是这种不合：词语、计划、成对的东西、整套哲学。

abstract.en: The word does not say wrong; it says out of tune.
abstract.cn: 这个词说的不是「错」，而是「走调」。

examples.en: It seemed absurd to carry an umbrella upside down in a storm.
examples.cn: 在暴风雨里把伞倒着拿，实在太荒唐。

examples.en: It is absurd to blame the weather for the delay.
examples.cn: 把延误归咎于天气是荒唐的。

examples.en: The court called the rule absurd.
examples.cn: 法院称这条规定荒谬。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿布瑟德」——阿布把伞倒扣在头上，还说自己最讲道理

root: 拉丁语 absurdus「走调的、刺耳的」← ab-（离开）+ surdus（聋的、迟钝的），由「不合调」引申为「不合理性」。关于 surdus 如何产生「不和谐」义，学界仍有不同解释。十六世纪经法语 absurde 进入英语。

sensesIntro.en: Four senses name what reason cannot accept: the laughable, the contrary to sense, the theatre of the absurd, and the logic that exposes nonsense.
sensesIntro.cn: 四个义项都指向理性无法接受的东西：可笑、违背常理、荒诞派戏剧，以及揭穿荒谬的逻辑方法。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one instrument playing a note that fits nothing else in the orchestra.
core.cn: 核心意象：一件乐器奏出一个与整个乐队都合不上的音。

branches.en: THE LAUGH: the mismatch makes one laugh.
branches.cn: 感受线：错位让人发笑。

branches.en: THE REASON: the thing contradicts ordinary sense.
branches.cn: 理性线：事情违背通常的道理。

branches.en: THE STAGE: a theatre built on meaninglessness.
branches.cn: 戏剧线：以无意义为根基的戏剧。

branches.en: THE LOGIC: a method that drives an idea to its ridiculous end.

senses.title: A large quantity
senses.definition: a quantity much greater than enough
senses.definitionCN: 远超所需的数量
senses.example: The orchard produced an abundance of apples that year.
senses.exampleCN: 那年果园的苹果获得了大丰收。
senses.why: The Latin verb means to overflow like a wave, and overflowing is the core sense.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁动词意为「如波浪般溢出」，溢出正是核心义。

senses.title: Wealth of resources
senses.definition: the state of having more than one needs
senses.definitionCN: 拥有超过所需之物的状态
senses.example: The region is known for its abundance of water.
senses.exampleCN: 这个地区以水资源丰富著称。
senses.why: A land that overflows with goods is called rich, and the noun names that plenty.
senses.whyCN: 物产 overflow 的地方被称作富庶，名词便指这种丰足。

senses.title: In abundance
senses.definition: in the phrase in abundance, existing in large amounts
senses.definitionCN: 在 in abundance 中，指大量存在
senses.example: Fish were found in abundance along the coast.
senses.exampleCN: 沿海一带鱼非常多。
senses.why: The preposition turns the noun into a measure of how something occurs.
senses.whyCN: 介词把名词变成描述事物出现方式的量度。

senses.title: Biological abundance
senses.definition: in ecology, the number of individuals in an area
senses.definitionCN: 生态学上指某地区的个体数量
senses.example: The survey measured the abundance of bees.
senses.exampleCN: 这项调查测量了蜜蜂的丰度。
senses.why: Science counts how much life fills a place, extending the old idea of plenty.
senses.whyCN: 科学计量一地生物之多，延续了古老的「丰盛」观念。

senses.title: An abundance of caution
senses.definition: in the phrase an abundance of caution, more care than usual
senses.definitionCN: 在 an abundance of caution 中，指超乎寻常的谨慎
senses.example: The bridge was closed out of an abundance of caution.
senses.exampleCN: 出于格外谨慎，这座桥被关闭了。
senses.why: Even a quality can be had in excess, and the phrase names that excess.
senses.whyCN: 连品质也可以过量，短语便指这种过量。

senses.title: Emotional abundance
senses.definition: a generous flow of feeling or kindness
senses.definitionCN: 情感或善意的充沛流露
senses.example: She greeted every guest with warmth and abundance.
senses.exampleCN: 她以温暖而充沛的热情迎接每位客人。
senses.why: What overflows need not be material, so the noun covers feeling too.
senses.whyCN: 溢出的不必是物质，名词也涵盖情感。

senses.title: An abundance mentality
senses.definition: the belief that there is enough for everyone
senses.definitionCN: 相信资源足够所有人分享的心态
senses.example: The team works well because of its abundance mentality.
senses.exampleCN: 这个团队合作良好，靠的是富足心态。
senses.why: A modern coinage treats plenty as a way of seeing the world.
senses.whyCN: 现代新造说法把「丰足」当成一种看世界的方式。

senses.title: Elemental abundance
senses.definition: in chemistry, how common an element is in a sample
senses.definitionCN: 化学上指某元素在样本中的常见程度
senses.example: The spectrograph reported the abundance of iron.
senses.exampleCN: 光谱仪报出了铁的丰度。
senses.why: Measuring how much of an element is present is another technical branch of plenty.
senses.whyCN: 测量某元素存在多少，是「丰盛」的另一技术分支。

senses.title: Existing in great number
senses.definition: is present in large numbers or amounts
senses.definitionCN: 以很大的数量或分量存在
senses.example: Fish were abundant in the clear lake.
senses.exampleCN: 清澈的湖里鱼很多。
senses.why: The Latin verb meant to overflow, and plenty is the first thing overflow gives.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁动词意为「溢出」，溢出首先带来的就是丰盛。

senses.title: Rich in a quality
senses.definition: contains a quality in large measure
senses.definitionCN: 大量含有某种特质
senses.example: The region is abundant in minerals.
senses.exampleCN: 该地区矿产丰富。
senses.why: Overflow can be of anything, so the word also measures qualities.
senses.whyCN: 溢出之物可以是任何东西，因此这个词也用来衡量品质。

senses.title: More than enough
senses.definition: is more than enough for a need
senses.definitionCN: 超过所需，十分充足
senses.example: We had abundant time to prepare.
senses.exampleCN: 我们有充裕的时间做准备。
senses.why: A wave that spills over the rim is the image of surplus.
senses.whyCN: 漫过边缘的浪，正是「有余」的意象。

senses.title: Rich in words
senses.definition: in writing, is full and generous in expression
senses.definitionCN: 在写作中表达充分而丰沛
senses.example: Her abundant prose filled every page.
senses.exampleCN: 她丰沛的文笔写满了每一页。
senses.why: Language can overflow too, and the word describes a full style.
senses.whyCN: 语言也会溢出，这个词便用来形容饱满的文风。

senses.title: Generous in amount
senses.definition: is given in a generous quantity, as rain or feeling
senses.definitionCN: 如雨水或情感，给得十分大方
senses.example: Abundant rain saved the harvest.
senses.exampleCN: 充沛的雨水挽救了收成。
senses.why: Nature's gifts that come in excess are called abundant.
senses.whyCN: 自然给的过多恩赐，就被称作 abundant。

senses.title: Growing thickly
senses.definition: of plants, grows thick and healthy
senses.definitionCN: 指植物长得茂密健壮
senses.example: Abundant grass covered the hillside.
senses.exampleCN: 茂盛的草覆盖着山坡。
senses.why: A field that overflows with growth shows the same image.
senses.whyCN: 长满草木的田野呈现的是同一个意象。

senses.title: Full of life
senses.definition: in religious or poetic use, means full and rich in life
senses.definitionCN: 在宗教或诗意用法中，指生命充实丰盈
senses.example: They spoke of abundant life as a gift.
senses.exampleCN: 他们谈论丰盛的生命，视之为恩赐。
senses.why: Overflow becomes a metaphor for a life that lacks nothing.
senses.whyCN: 溢出成了「一无所缺的生活」的隐喻。

senses.title: An abundant number
senses.definition: in mathematics, is a number smaller than the sum of its divisors
senses.definitionCN: 数学上指小于其真因数之和的数
senses.example: Twelve is an abundant number.
senses.exampleCN: 十二是一个过剩数。
senses.why: The divisors add up beyond the number itself, an exact overflow.
senses.whyCN: 因数之和超过了这个数本身，正是一种精确的溢出。

entries.definition: the quality of being abusive.
entries.definitionCN: 辱骂性；虐待性。

entries.definition: offensive and humiliating in speech.
entries.definitionCN: 言语上冒犯且羞辱人的。

entries.definition: causing pain deliberately, without the misuse idea.
entries.definitionCN: 蓄意造成痛苦，不含「错用」观念。

entries.definition: violent and aggressive, often of attacks or temper.
entries.definitionCN: 恶毒凶暴的，常指攻击或脾气。

entries.definition: disparaging, lowering someone's standing in words.
entries.definitionCN: 贬损性的，以言辞贬低他人。

entries.definition: showing due regard for others; the opposite manner.
entries.definitionCN: 表示敬重的；态度上的反面。

normalIntro.en: Chain the word to abuse and the use root.
normalIntro.cn: 把该词与 abuse 及 use 词根串起来记。

normal.en: ab- away + use = using wrongly.
normal.cn: ab- 偏离 + use 使用 = 错用、滥用。

normal.en: -ive makes it an adjective of habitual behavior.
normal.cn: -ive 使之成为描述惯常行为的形容词。

normal.en: Two faces: abusive words, abusive hands.
normal.cn: 两副面孔：恶语伤人，暴力伤身。

normal.en: Third face: abusive use of power and drugs.
normal.cn: 第三副面孔：权力与药物的滥用。

normal.en: Family: abuse, abusive, abusively, abusiveness.
normal.cn: 词族：abuse、abusive、abusively、abusiveness。

abstract.en: Hear the shout that cuts like glass.
abstract.cn: 听那如利刃割人般的怒喝。

abstract.en: Picture a door slammed again and again.
abstract.cn: 想象一扇门被一次次砸响。

abstract.en: See a stamp misused on an official document.
abstract.cn: 看一枚公章被盖在不该盖的文件上。

examples.en: The forum bans users who post abusive comments.
examples.cn: 论坛封禁发布辱骂评论的用户。

examples.en: He grew up in an abusive household and never spoke of it.
examples.cn: 他在施暴的家庭中长大，对此只字未提。

examples.en: The report criticized the abusive use of emergency funds.
examples.cn: 报告批评了应急资金的滥用。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「我别耍事」——喝酒后别耍酒疯说狠事，那是辱骂虐待。

root: 拉丁语 abuti 的分词 abusus → 古法语 abus → 英语 abuse → 加 -ive 构成 abusive。词根 uti「使用」（同根：use、usage、usual）。核心义「错用」，引申为言语错用（辱骂）、行为错用（虐待）、权力错用（滥用）。

sensesIntro.en: Misuse branches into cruel words, cruel acts, and corrupt use of power.
sensesIntro.cn: 「错用」分出恶语、苛行与滥权三枝。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: something good used in the wrong way until it harms.
core.cn: 核心意象：好东西被用错了地方，直至伤人。

branches.en: SPEECH: insults and curses are language misused.
branches.cn: 言语：侮辱与咒骂是被错用的语言。

branches.en: BODIES: repeated harm marks an abusive person or home.
branches.cn: 身体：反复伤害标记施暴者或施暴之家。

branches.en: OFFICE AND SUBSTANCE: power and drugs taken against their purpose.
branches.cn: 职权与药物：被用于背离本旨。

branches.en: RELATIONSHIP FRAME: both senses describe repeated conduct toward persons.
branches.cn: 关系框架：两义都描述对人的持续行为。

branches.en: LEGAL REGISTER: courts and codes name conduct abusive.
branches.cn: 法律语域：法典与判例称此类行为为 abusive。

intro.en: The uti root of use builds a family from neutral to harmful.
intro.cn: use 的词根 uti 构建了从中性到贬义的词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin compounds of uti keep the using idea alive.
latinIntro.cn: uti 的拉丁复合词让「使用」观念延续。

derivatives.zh: 基础词，义为「虐待；滥用」
副词，义为「辱骂地」
名词，义为「辱骂性；虐待性」

definition_zh: 毗邻；紧靠；与……接界
definition_en: to touch or border on something along an edge
core_image: 两堵墙的边线贴在一起，中间没有缝隙
scene: 测绘员沿地界走了一圈，指着篱笆说，这块地正好贴着后面的林地。Their garden abuts the edge of the forest.
sceneCN: 这里 abut 是「毗邻、接界」（第 1 个义项：土地沿边界相接）；句意为他们的花园紧贴着森林边缘。

derivatives.zh: 由本词加名词后缀构成，义为「桥台；支承结构」
由动词加现在分词后缀构成，义为「紧邻的、毗连的」

senses.title: To border on land
senses.definition: of land or a building, to touch another property along a boundary
senses.definitionCN: 指土地或建筑沿边界与另一处相接
senses.example: Their farm abuts the nature reserve on the north side.
senses.exampleCN: 他们的农场北侧紧靠自然保护区。
senses.why: Middle English abuten came from a word meaning 'to end at', so the verb marks where one property ends against another.
senses.whyCN: 中古英语 abuten 来自意为「止于」的词，因此这个动词标记一块地产止于另一块的位置。

senses.title: To meet and bear against
senses.definition: of structural parts, to meet and support one another
senses.definitionCN: 指结构部件相互接触并承托
senses.example: The arch abuts the stone piers on both sides.
senses.exampleCN: 拱体抵住两侧的石墩。
senses.why: Builders speak of one part abutting another when two edges meet under load, which is why the supporting block is called an abutment.
senses.whyCN: 建筑者用「一部分抵住另一部分」描述两边在受力下相接，因此承托的砌块被称为 abutment（桥台）。

intro.en: Abut comes from Middle English abuten, 'to end at or border on', and survives mainly in property and building descriptions.
intro.cn: abut 来自中古英语 abuten（止于、接界），现今主要用于地产与建筑描写。

items.en: bouter meant 'to push, thrust', from a Germanic source.
items.cn: bouter 意为「推、顶」，源自日耳曼语。

items.en: abuten combined a prefix with bouter and meant 'to end at'.
items.cn: abuten 由前缀与 bouter 结合，意为「止于」。

items.en: Property law adopted abut for land that touches another holding.
items.cn: 财产法采用 abut 指与另一块地产相接的土地。

items.en: Builders used abut for parts that meet and carry load.
items.cn: 建筑用语用 abut 指相接并承重的部件。

items.en: The noun abutment named the masonry that receives the thrust of an arch.
items.cn: 名词 abutment 指承受拱推力的砌体。

items.en: Modern usage keeps the verb in surveying, planning, and structural writing.
items.cn: 现代用法把这个动词保留在测量、规划与结构写作中。

note.en: The first group gathers forms of the same small family; the second gathers verbs for neighbouring and touching.
note.cn: 第一组收同一小词族的各种形式；第二组收表示相邻与接触的动词。

entries.definition: The supporting structure at the end of a bridge or arch.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「桥台」，桥或拱端的承托结构。

entries.definition: The participle used as an adjective for adjoining property.
entries.definitionCN: 分词作形容词，义为「紧邻的」。

entries.definition: The past tense, common in surveys of boundaries.
entries.definitionCN: 过去式，常用于边界测量。

entries.definition: A verb meaning to lie next to a boundary.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「与……接界」。

entries.definition: A verb meaning to be next to or joined with.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「毗连、邻接」。

entries.definition: A verb meaning to come into contact with.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「接触」。

entries.definition: A verb meaning to be situated next to.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「邻近」。

normalIntro.en: The normal hooks use the surveying image and the fixed prepositions; the abstract hooks picture two boundary lines pressed together.
normalIntro.cn: 常规记忆点用测量意象与固定介词；抽象记忆点想象两条边界线压在一起。

normal.en: Abut is mostly a property word: land abuts land.
normal.cn: abut 主要是地产用词：土地紧邻土地。

normal.en: The usual prepositions are on and against.
normal.cn: 常用介词是 on 与 against。

normal.en: The noun abutment names the block that takes an arch's push.
normal.cn: 名词 abutment 指承受拱推力的砌块。

normal.en: The double t stays doubled before -ed and -ing.
normal.cn: 加 -ed 与 -ing 时双写 t。

normal.en: Adjoin is the more common synonym in general writing.
normal.cn: 在一般写作中 adjoin 是更常见的同义词。

abstract.en: Picture two garden fences sharing one line with no gap.
abstract.cn: 想象两道篱笆共用一条线，中间没有缝隙。

abstract.en: Picture an arch pressing its weight into stone piers.
abstract.cn: 想象拱把重量压进石墩。

abstract.en: Picture a surveyor walking the edge where field meets forest.
abstract.cn: 想象测量员走在田野与森林相接的边上。

examples.en: The warehouse abuts the railway line.
examples.cn: 仓库紧靠铁路线。

examples.en: Rooms abutting the courtyard have no outside windows.
examples.cn: 紧邻庭院的房间没有外窗。

examples.en: The new road will abut the western boundary of the site.
examples.cn: 新路将紧贴场地的西侧边界。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿巴特」——两块地的边线贴在一起，谁也不留缝，就是毗邻。

root: 古法语 bouter（推、顶）→ 中古英语 abuten（止于）；核心义是「边界抵到另一处」

sensesIntro.en: The senses move from land that ends against other land, to structural parts that meet under load.
sensesIntro.cn: 这些义项从止于另一块土地的地产，走到在受力下相接的结构部件。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two edges pressed together without a gap
core.cn: 核心意象：两条边压在一起，没有缝隙

branches.en: One property ending where another begins.
branches.cn: 一块地产止于另一块开始处。

branches.en: Building parts that meet and carry thrust.
branches.cn: 相接并承受推力的建筑部件。

branches.en: In both senses one edge stops against another.
branches.cn: 两个义项都是一条边抵在另一条边上。

branches.en: The bridge abutment is the built form of the same meeting.
branches.cn: 桥台是这种相接的建筑形态。

branches.en: Surveying and masonry share one verb of contact.
branches.cn: 测量与砌筑共用同一个表示接触的动词。

intro.en: The word is short and mostly indivisible; its family grows with the agent noun abutment and the participial adjective abutting.
intro.cn: 这个词很短且基本不可再分；词族以名词 abutment 与分词形容词 abutting 生长。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin ancestor; the word came through Old French from a Germanic pushing verb, so the Latin entries are left empty.
latinIntro.cn: 它没有拉丁语祖先；该词经古法语来自日耳曼语表示「推」的动词，因此拉丁条目留空。
